points.point: Kejriwal raised the 2010-11 Sesa Goa/Sterlite precedent on mining-lease transfers; Deshnee Naidoo confirmed bauxite (Sijimali) and coal mining licences must be transferred to Vedanta Aluminium as part of a parallel approvals plan.
points.quote: Ashish, you are right. This is part of the overall approvals that we have in our sight.

points.point: Two legal obstacles surfaced: the second motion hearing was part-heard on July 2 with the next date August 20, and NCLAT granted an interim stay on the TSPL power demerger order (backed by a Rs. 1,248 crore cash-backed bank guarantee).

rationale.rationale: Management's stated reason is structural: Anant Raj Limited (ARL) today runs two unrelated verticals — a real estate and infrastructure business, and a data centre and cloud services business — and the Data Centre Business is currently split across two entities (ARL itself and its wholly owned subsidiary ARCPL), with assets, employees, investments and operations housed in both. The Composite Scheme therefore does two things in sequence: first amalgamates ARCPL into ARL (no shares issued, since ARCPL is a 100% subsidiary with 25,00,000 shares held by ARL), then demerges the consolidated Data Centre Business out of ARL into Ashok Cloud Private Limited (ACPL), whose business is described as data centre and co-location services, sovereign public cloud, AI-ready cloud infrastructure, DC & DR services, cloud migration and data backup. The problems management says this solves are: (a) a fragmented, intra-group ownership structure, which consolidation simplifies and lets intra-group arrangements be cancelled or rationalised; (b) the data centre business being valued inside a real estate company despite a 'distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding requirements', which a separate listing is meant to fix through independent, market-driven recognition and valuation; (c) inability to raise sector-specific capital and pursue data-centre-specific strategic investments and partnerships while buried inside ARL; and (d) divided management attention, which the Scheme replaces with dedicated management focus and decision-making per vertical. The scale disclosure supports the 'hidden inside real estate' argument: for the year to March 31, 2026, the demerged undertaking's turnover is ₹145.90 crore against total turnover of ₹1,627.72 crore, i.e. 8.96% (computed after aggregating ARCPL and ARL post-merger). ARL shareholders are kept whole economically — 1 ACPL share of ₹2 face value for every ARL share of ₹2, giving them 49% directly while ARL retains 51%, so post-scheme ACPL is 79.14% promoter-held (ARL 51% plus ARL promoters 28.14%) and 20.86% public, and ARL's own shareholding pattern is unchanged at 57.42% promoter / 42.58% public across 35,98,76,930 shares. ACPL is to be listed on BSE and NSE via a Rule 19(7) exemption under the SEBI Scheme of Arrangement master circular dated June 20, 2023, with the Board approving on July 21, 2026 and NCLT approval sought under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013.
rationale.evolution: No evolution can be reconstructed from the material supplied: the 'CALL PASSAGES' section of the prompt was empty, so there are no earnings-call passages (and no call dates or labels) in the record. The only dated points available are the financial reference date of March 31, 2026 for the turnover split (₹145.90 crore of ₹1,627.72 crore) and the Board's approval of the Composite Scheme on July 21, 2026, announced the same day by press release as creating 'Two Focused Independent Listed Companies'. Within the filing itself the plan is already in final two-step form — ARCPL merged into ARL, then the Data Centre Business demerged into Ashok Cloud — with no earlier variant described.

points.point: The starting problem: two unrelated verticals inside one listed company, with the data centre business itself split across ARL and its subsidiary ARCPL (assets, employees, investments and operations in both).
points.quote: The Anant Raj Limited presently operates two distinct business verticals, namely: (i) a real estate business; and (ii) a data centre and cloud services business ("Data Centre Business").

points.point: Management says the data centre business has outgrown its position inside ARL and can run its own growth path as a separate listed entity, while still trading on ARL's brand and goodwill.
points.quote: The Data Centre Business has evolved significantly over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity focused on the rapidly growing Data Centre Business whilst continuing to leverage ARL's institutional strengths, strong brand equity and goodwill.

points.point: Valuation rationale: a separate listing is meant to get the data centre business recognised and valued on its own operating profile, growth, risk-return profile and funding needs rather than as part of a real estate company.
points.quote: the segregation of the Data Centre Business into a separately listed company would facilitate independent market recognition and valuation of the Data Centre Business, having regard to its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding requirements

points.point: Structural cleanup rationale: consolidating the business out of two entities into one simplifies ownership and allows intra-group arrangements to be cancelled or rationalised.
points.quote: consolidation of the Data Centre Business, resulting in a simpler ownership structure, streamlined operations and cancellation or rationalization of intra-group arrangements

points.point: Capital and partnership rationale: as a standalone legal entity, Ashok Cloud can raise sector-specific capital and resources and pursue data-centre-specific strategic investments and partnerships.
points.quote: the separation of the Data Centre Business into a distinct legal entity will enable Ashok Cloud to effectively attract sector specific resources for its growth requirements and pursue strategic investments, partnerships, thereby unlocking greater value for its shareholders

points.point: Focus rationale: each management team gets to set strategy for its own vertical instead of sharing decision-making across real estate and data centres.
points.quote: the Scheme will enable dedicated management focus and decision-making for each business vertical, allowing the management teams of ARL and Ashok Cloud to pursue business strategies and growth initiatives tailored to their respective operational and market requirements.

points.point: The size disclosure: the demerged data centre undertaking is ₹145.90 crore of turnover against ₹1,627.72 crore total, 8.96%, for the year to March 31, 2026 (after aggregating ARCPL with ARL).
points.quote: Turnover* (in Crores) Demerged Undertaking 145.90 Total 1627.72 Percentage 8.96%

points.point: What the demerged business actually is: colocation, sovereign public cloud, AI-ready cloud infrastructure, DC & DR, cloud migration and backup — i.e. operating services, not property.
points.quote: ACPL is inter alia engaged in the business of providing data centre and Co-Location services, sovereign public cloud services and AI ready Cloud Infrastructure, DC & DR services, including cloud migration, data backup solutions and other allied activities.

points.point: Step one is a no-consideration internal merger: ARCPL, a wholly owned subsidiary (25,00,000 shares, 100% held by ARL), folds into ARL with no shares issued.
points.quote: Since, the Amalgamating Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Amalgamated Company, no shares of the Amalgamated Company shall be issued or allotted in consideration of Part II of the Composite Scheme i.e. the merger of ARCPL with and into ARL.

points.point: Shareholders are made direct owners of 49% of ACPL on a 1:1 share basis, with ARL retaining 51%; post-scheme ACPL is 79.14% promoter (ARL 51% + ARL promoters 28.14%) and 20.86% public, while ARL's 57.42/42.58 pattern is unchanged.
points.quote: the existing shareholders of ARL shall receive shares in Ashok Cloud (ACPL) pursuant to the demerger, thereby enabling them to directly participate in the future growth and value creation potential of the Data Centre business through a dedicated and focused listed entity, while benefiting from independent market-driven valuation

points.point: ACPL's shares are to be listed on BSE and NSE without an IPO, using a Rule 19(7) exemption under the SEBI Scheme of Arrangement master circular of June 20, 2023; ACPL also stays an ARL subsidiary.
points.quote: the existing shares of ARL in ACPL shall be listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited by seeking exemption under Rule 19(7) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957

points.point: The July 21, 2026 press release frames the outcome as two focused listed companies — ARL in real estate and infrastructure, Ashok Cloud in next-generation data centre and cloud services including AI workloads.
points.quote: The restructuring will  enable each business to pursue focused growth strategies  and will unlock shareholder value.

rationale.what_management_expects: ARL: a pure real estate and infrastructure developer with its own tailored strategy and unchanged shareholding. Ashok Cloud: a dedicated listed data centre, cloud and AI-workload entity with independent market-driven valuation, sector-specific capital and partnerships, a simpler post-consolidation structure, and dedicated management focus. Shareholders: 100% of ACPL's economic interest (49% direct, 51% via ARL) and unlocked shareholder value. No margin or return targets are given.
rationale.gaps: No earnings-call passages were supplied at all. The filing gives no margins, capex, MW capacity, debt or asset allocation, timeline, or any investor, lender or partner request driving it.

The only separation referred to is historical and belongs to another group: a court-approved demerger in 2011 under which the power business was separated from the erstwhile Indiabulls Group, after which Sinnar Thermal Power Limited (STPL) has been part of the Ratan India Group. rationale.rationale: Note on the premise: in this filing HSCL is not separating out one of its own businesses — it is the Resulting Company receiving a business. The Scheme of Arrangement (Sections 230–232, Companies Act 2013), approved by HSCL's Board on 21 September 2026, demerges the 'Tyre Business of DBRL' from Dalmia Bharat Refractories Limited (Demerged Company) into Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd (Resulting Company) as a going concern on an 'as is where is' basis, with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026 (or such other date as the NCLT may approve). The Demerged Undertaking comprises all assets, liabilities, contracts, employees, brands, trademarks, licences, permits, approvals and properties attributable to the Tyre Business, defined as designing, manufacturing and development of all types of tyre and tyre products; its turnover as on 31 March 2026 was INR 149.31 crores, or 3.39% of HSCL's total turnover for FY ended 31 March 2026. The Board's stated reasoning is that, given the nature of the Demerged Undertaking, its future requirements and the respective strengths and strategic objectives of HSCL, the demerger gives the Tyre Business 'more focused ownership and robust operating structure' while letting each company direct management attention, capital and resources to businesses aligned with its own capabilities. For HSCL specifically the filing lists six benefits: forward-integration of the Tyre Business with its existing carbon black and advanced carbon materials business to strengthen its presence across the tyre value chain; leverage of its material expertise, R&D, manufacturing and customer relationships for product customisation and expansion across tyre application segments; operational and commercial synergies in raw material sourcing, product development, manufacturing, logistics, distribution, market development, shared services and customer engagement; direct ownership and control enabling coordinated capacity utilisation, modernisation, product expansion and distribution build-out; greater strategic and financial flexibility to align investment, funding and capacity expansion with group strategy; and long-term growth and value creation for HSCL and its stakeholders. Consideration is non-cash: HSCL will issue 1 new equity share of face value INR 1 for every 260 DBRL shares of face value INR 10, per a 20 September 2026 joint valuation report by SSPA & Co and CA Manish Gadia, with a fairness opinion of the same date from Jajodia Equity Advisors Services Limited. The dilution is minimal — HSCL promoter holding moves from 52.49% to 52.47% and public from 47.51% to 47.53% (total shares 50,45,74,175 to 50,47,50,637, plus 53,896 exercisable ESOPs) — and DBRL's own shareholding pattern (promoter 74.99%, public 25.01%) does not change.

The only datable sequence in the supplied material is internal to the filing: the joint valuation report and the merchant banker's fairness opinion are both dated 20 September 2026; HSCL's Board approved the Scheme at its meeting on 21 September 2026 and disclosed it to BSE and NSE under Regulation 30 on the same date (Ref. No. HSCL/Stock-Ex/2026-27/59); the Appointed Date is set at 1 October 2026, subject to NCLT; and the sizing is measured against FY ended 31 March 2026. No earlier or alternative version of the plan is described.

In it, two wholly-owned subsidiaries of the listed parent are being merged into their holding company and dissolved: Dealskart Online Services Private Limited (incorporated 8 September 2011, CIN U74140DL2011PTC224819, PAN AADCD9571D), which provides operations and maintenance (O&M) services to the parent's omni-channel stores PAN India, and Lenskart Eyetech Private Limited (incorporated 2 July 2015, CIN U74110DL2015PTC282327, PAN AACCL8854C), which operates training centres for retail staff. The Transferee Company is Lenskart Solutions Limited (originally incorporated 19 May 2008 as Valyoo Technologies Private Limited, renamed on conversion to a public company on 16 June 2025, CIN L33100DL2008PLC178355), a listed entity on NSE and BSE, engaged in designing, manufacturing, branding and retailing eyewear, and the holding company of both transferors. The only stated motive visible in the excerpt is tax and legal form: the scheme is drawn to comply with the conditions for an 'amalgamation' under Section 2(6) of the Income Tax Act, 2025 and other applicable provisions. The structural plumbing is set out as Parts A–E, covering introduction and rationale, share capital, amalgamation of the transferors into the transferee, consideration, accounting treatment and dissolution of the transferors, and general terms. Beyond this, the substantive 'Purpose and Rationale' clauses of Part A are cut off by the truncation, so no synergy, margin, capital, focus, valuation, investor, lender or partner rationale is stated anywhere in the supplied material. rationale.rationale: Pricol's board (approval announced June 27, 2026) is demerging its Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions ('DICVS') undertaking — driver information systems including connected, electronic, mechanical and electro-mechanical instrument clusters, integrated infotainment, advanced e-cockpit solutions, telematics, battery management systems and a few sensors — into Pricol Autotech Limited, leaving Pricol Limited with the Actuation, Control & Fluid Management Systems ('ACFMS') and Precision Products ('P3L') businesses. The scale cited is material: DICVS turnover of INR 2,424.63 crores for FY ending March 31, 2026, or 61.17% of consolidated turnover, with management stating both halves have 'acquired sufficient scale and maturity to function more effectively as focused standalone businesses.' The stated problem is that the two sides operate with differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles inside one structure, which creates operational complexity, slow decision-making, and shared processes, policies, systems and governance that fit neither business. The fix is two focused platforms — an automotive technology entity and an automotive & industrial precision engineering entity — each with dedicated management, independent capital allocation, and its own governance, described as 'simpler, sharper and more agile' to meet fast-changing technology needs and dynamic market realities. Capital-markets reasoning is explicit: clearer visibility of each business's stakeholder value, growth prospects and investment merits, improved ability to attract strategic and financial investors, greater flexibility to access capital, and unlocking shareholder value. Mechanically it is value-neutral at the shareholder level — no cash consideration, 1:1 share entitlement (1 Pricol Autotech share of INR 1 face value per Pricol share), no change in Pricol's shareholding pattern, and Pricol Autotech's register mirroring Pricol's at 38.51% promoter / 61.49% public, with listing sought on NSE and BSE. Valuation rests on SSPA & Co's Share Entitlement Ratio Report dated 27th June 2026, with a fairness opinion from Saffron Capital Advisors.
rationale.evolution: No earnings call passages were supplied in this prompt — the 'CALL PASSAGES' section is empty, so the call-by-call emergence of the idea cannot be reconstructed from these texts. The only dated evidence here is the scheme filing itself: board approval of the scheme of arrangement announced Coimbatore, June 27th, 2026, with the share entitlement ratio report of the same date (27th June 2026). The filing's own framing — 'Over the years' the DICVS business 'has evolved into a differentiated platform,' and 'Over time with a well thoughtout and clear strategic intent' both businesses reached standalone scale — implies a multi-year build-up to the decision, but the filing does not date those earlier steps.

points.point: The demerged undertaking is the DICVS business, and the filing quantifies it as the majority of the group: INR 2,424.63 crores of turnover in FY ending March 31, 2026, equal to 61.17% of consolidated turnover.
points.quote: The turnover of the DICVS Business for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, stood at INR 2,424.63 crores. This represents 61.17% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2026.

points.point: Stated strategic motive: build a simpler, sharper, more agile entity able to keep pace with the technology cycle and market conditions specific to DICVS.
points.quote: The demerger of the DICVS Business is a strategic decision to create a simpler, sharper and more agile corporate entity, to meet the fast changing needs and technologies related to this business and its dynamic market realities.

points.point: The core problem named is mismatch inside one company — the two businesses differ on customers, competition, capital allocation and risk, and each has now reached standalone scale.
points.quote: The Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business of the Demerged Company currently operates with differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles.

points.point: Both halves are said to have outgrown the combined structure, which is the filing's justification for separating now rather than earlier.
points.quote: Over time with a well thoughtout and clear strategic intent, both the Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business of the Demerged Company have acquired sufficient scale and maturity to function more effectively as focused standalone businesses .

points.point: Benefit list includes independent capital allocation and faster decision-making via reduced complexity, plus dedicated management teams for each business.
points.quote: Financial flexibility for each entity to pursue investment decisions aligned with their respective business portfolios and market requirements ;

points.point: Explicit investor-facing rationale: separate platforms should make each business's value and growth visible and make it easier to attract strategic and financial investors and access capital.
points.quote: Creation of focused and independent business platforms for the Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business of the Demerged Company, with clear and enhanced visibility of their respective stakeholder value, growth prospects and investment merits, improved abilit y to attract strategic and financial investors to meet the needs of the respective business, greater flexibility to access capital, pursue growth and technology opportunities and implement their respective long -term strategies .

points.point: The structure created is two named platforms — an automotive technology entity (Pricol Autotech, DICVS) and an automotive & industrial precision engineering entity (Pricol Limited, holding ACFMS and P3L).
points.quote: Strategic demerger to create two focused  business platform s – an Automotive Technology Entity and an Automotive  & Industrial  Precision Engineering Entity, for a simpler, sharper and more agile structure meeting the fast -changing technological needs and the dynamic market realities

points.point: DICVS is characterised as having evolved into a differentiated platform needing its own long-term strategy, technology capabilities and partnerships for integrated solutions.
points.quote: The proposed demerger  recognises this evolution and enables the business to pursue independent long -term strategies, strengthen technology capabilities , partnerships for integrated solution offerings  and respond more effectively to changing industry dynamics.

points.point: Retained-business case: ACFMS is backed by growing domestic and export footprints in fluid management and control, and P3L is positioned for expanding precision components demand.
points.quote: The ACFMS and P3L businesses will continue to remain part of Pricol  Limited, with the ACFMS business being supported by growing domestic and export footprint s and opportunities in fluid management and control  solutions , and the P3L business being strategically positioned to capitali se on the expanding opportunity in precision  components.

points.point: Consideration is a value-neutral mirror split: no cash, 1:1 entitlement, Pricol Autotech's shareholding mirroring Pricol's (promoters 38.51%, public 61.49% post-scheme), with listing sought on NSE and BSE.
points.quote: Shareholders of Pricol Limited will receive one fully paid -up equity share of Pricol Autotech Limited for every one fully paid -up equity share held in Pricol Limited (1:1 share entitlement ratio) , resulting in the shareholding of Pricol Autotech Limited mirroring the shareholding of Pricol Limited , subject to the Scheme becoming effective.

points.point: CMD Vikram Mohan frames timing as businesses having diverged on customers, technology priorities, capital requirements and growth, making independent operation right now.
points.quote: Over the years, our businesses have evolved into strong and differentiated platforms with distinct customer needs, technology priorities , capital requirements  and growth opportunities.

points.point: Valuation and fairness are documented: SSPA & Co's share entitlement ratio report dated 27th June 2026 with a fairness opinion from SEBI-registered merchant banker Saffron Capital Advisors.
points.quote: The share entitlement ratio has been arrived basis the Share Entitlement  Ratio Report dated 27th June 2026 issued by SSPA & Co, Chartered Accountants , Registered  Valuer.

rationale.rationale: Refex Industries Ltd. (RIL) is separating its green mobility (EV passenger transport) business from its core Ash & Coal handling business through a two-step composite scheme: first the amalgamation of its wholly owned subsidiary Refex Green Mobility Limited (RGML) into RIL, then the demerger of the Green Mobility Business Undertaking out of RIL into Refex Mobility Limited (RML), which will be independently listed parallel to RIL with mirror shareholding (no valuation exercise was required because RGML is a 100% subsidiary). The stated reason is structural dissimilarity: the scheme says the nature of risk and competition, financial profiles and return ratios of the Ash & Coal handling business are distinct from the Green Mobility Business, which is 'capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders.' Housing an asset-light, cash-generating ash/coal services business (management and an analyst put ash and coal at more than 96% of revenue; Anil Jain said standalone RIL will be 95–100% ash and coal) alongside a fleet business still building scale blurs both stories, so the scheme targets an 'independent global scale company' in mobility, greater management focus in each entity, the ability for investors to hold the two risk profiles separately, and 'focused and sharper capital market access (debt and equity).' Practically, RML takes roughly Rs.220 crores of net assets off RIL's consolidated balance sheet and, per Anil Jain, 'all the debt etc. will also move to that entity,' giving mobility 'more liberty to do its own business' and strategic and financial flexibility; RIL's results will no longer consolidate mobility. The separation sits inside a wider portfolio cleanup in the same period — a strategic call to exit power trading (wound up because 'the margins in power trading were extremely low and this was not in alignment' with the company's focus) and the refrigerant gas business, 'in order to achieve stronger return profiles by redeploying capital and focus towards core businesses.' Lenders are an explicit gating party: in January 2026 the company was 'waiting for some final NOCs from the lenders' before the scheme could be filed. Mobility itself is presented as credible standalone: over INR100 crores of revenue in three years of operation, improving utilization and unit economics, 'steadily progressing towards profitability.' Wind (Venwind Refex Power, Rs.1,860 crores cumulative order book) is explicitly not part of the separation and stays with RIL alongside ash and coal.
rationale.evolution: On the Nov 6, 2025 call the demerger first surfaced as an in-progress composite scheme, framed as unlocking 'focused value creation,' with management deflecting a valuation question (no valuation needed — 100% subsidiary, mirror shareholding) and noting mobility results would stop consolidating. By Jan 21, 2026 it had become concrete and conditional: final lender NOCs pending before filing, NCLT completion guided for end-April, Rs.220 crores of net assets and all mobility debt moving to RML, and RIL recast as a 95–100% ash-and-coal standalone, alongside the fresh decision to exit power trading and refrigerant gases. By the May 27, 2026 (Jun 2026) call the rationale had been restated in capital-allocation language — 'sharper operational focus, clear capital allocation and stronger long-term value discovery' — while the timeline slipped to an NCLT hearing in the first week of June and another 60–75 days, with management insisting its own compliances were 100% done and the delay was purely court process (summer vacation).

points.point: Management formally introduced the separation as a two-step composite scheme — RGML merging into RIL, then the Mobility Undertaking demerging into a separately listed Refex Mobility Limited — framed as unlocking focused value for stakeholders.
points.quote: On this note, I would like to briefly mention that the de-merger of Refex Green Mobility Limited from Refex Industries Limited is in progress through a composite scheme comprising two steps.

points.point: The purpose given for mobility post-separation was independence of strategy and funding, not a trade sale or fundraise disclosed at that point.
points.quote: Post-demerger, the mobility vertical will pursue its growth plan independently with strategic and financial flexibility.

points.point: Asked by Smit Jain what valuation had been ascribed to the mobility vertical, CFO Dinesh Kumar Agarwal said none was required because RGML is a 100% subsidiary and shareholders get mirror shareholding in the new entity.
points.quote: As per the company and the process of merger and demerger process there is no valuations requirement to be done since the company holds 100, it is a 100 subsidiary and a mirror shareholding will happen, all the shareholder of Refex Industries Limited will be same shareholding as per the scheme which has been dis

points.point: On a question about ash and coal being over 96% of revenue and future segment margins, Anil Jain said mobility will stop being consolidated once listed, so RIL's reported mix becomes ash/coal plus wind (whose EBITDA margins he said are not very different).
points.quote: Like we said that we are demerging the mobility business so hopefully in the next few months it will be a separate listed entity and the results will not get consolidated after that.

points.point: The same focus logic was applied to power trading, which was wound up entirely on margin and strategic-fit grounds — evidence the demerger is part of a broader portfolio pruning.
points.quote: We have decided to wind this up completely because the margins in power trading were extremely low and this was not in alignment with what we were doing where our majority of focus was.

points.point: Opening remarks tied the separation to a wider capital-redeployment and return-profile agenda, announcing exits from power trading and refrigerant gases alongside the mobility demerger (Q3 PBT Rs.89 crores, up 24% QoQ; PAT Rs.67 crores, up 29% QoQ).
points.quote: In order to achieve stronger return profiles by redeploying capital and focus towards core businesses, the management has taken a strategic call to exit power trading and refrigerant gas business.

points.point: Answering Ananya Khanna of Alpha Alternatives on timeline and synergies, Anil Jain disclosed lenders as the gating item — final NOCs awaited before the scheme could be filed — and that mobility's debt travels with it; Dinesh Agarwal guided to April completion.
points.quote: Once it is demerged, the Refex Mobility will run as a separate entity where it will have more liberty to do its own business and also it will have its own, all the debt etc. will also move to that entity.

points.point: Pressed by individual investor Vivek Joshi on how assets split, Dinesh Agarwal quantified the transfer at Rs.220 crores of net assets and stressed RIL itself owns no RGML assets — it is a 100% subsidiary going to parallel separate listing.
points.quote: Okay. So from the net assets, Rs.220 Crores get transferred to Mobility, right?

points.point: Asked about the 3–5 year business mix, Anil Jain said standalone RIL becomes almost purely ash and coal handling, with mobility entirely out of consolidation and wind the other consolidated growth leg.
points.quote: Officially, on a standalone basis, Refex industries will have 100% business, maybe 95% business from ash and coal handling only.

points.point: Management restated the rationale in capital-allocation terms and said key regulatory and procedural milestones were already achieved, with the process on track for operational separation.
points.quote: We believe this structure will create sharper operational focus, clear capital allocation and stronger long-term value discovery for all the stakeholders.

points.point: Mobility was presented as standalone-viable: INR100 crores+ revenue in three years, improving utilization and operating efficiency, moving toward profitability — supporting the case for an independent listing.
points.quote: Operationally, the mobility business continues to witness strong growth momentum and has crossed INR100 crores revenue this year with just 3 years of operation.

points.point: Asked by Vidyashankar R whether the demerger was stuck at NCLT or blocked by something else, Dinesh Agarwal said there is no challenge, only court process — hearing expected first week of June, completion in another 60–75 days, with all company-side compliances done.
points.quote: if we put a time line, another 60 to 75 days, this should get completed.

points.point: On funding the separation and renewables scale-up, the CFO said refinancing was done in the quarter to lower borrowing cost (with temporary processing charges) at both Venwind and RIL, and that capital is not a constraint.
points.quote: We have sufficient internal accrual and also the bank balance to fund the current and the future capital requirements.

points.point: The filing's core argument is dissimilarity of the two businesses on risk, competition, financial profile and return ratios — the structural reason they should not share one balance sheet or one equity story.
points.quote: The nature of risk and competition, financial profiles and return ratios involved in the Ash & Coal handling business of RIL are distinct from Green Mobility Business presently undertaken through its wholly owned subsidiary RGML.

points.point: The filing names the constituencies asking for separation — a different investor, lender and strategic-partner set for green mobility — as the reason to list it parallel to RIL rather than keep it as a subsidiary.
points.quote: The Green Mobility Business is capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders and have significant potential for growth and profitability.

points.point: Listed benefits include creating an independent global-scale mobility company, greater management focus in each business, independent collaboration, and letting investors choose exposure by risk profile.
points.quote: Creation of an independent global scale company focusing exclusively on Green Mobility Business Undertaking and taking advantage of the growth potential in the said respective sector;

points.point: The financing motive is explicit: separate, sharper access to both debt and equity markets as the mechanism for unlocking mobility's value; the scheme also asserts no added burden or prejudice to shareholders or creditors.
points.quote: Enabling focused and sharper capital market access (debt and equity) and thereby unlocking the value of the Green Mobility Business Undertaking and creating enhanced value for shareholders.

rationale.what_management_expects: RIL becomes a near-pure ash & coal handler — 95–100% of standalone revenue — with capital redeployed from exited power trading and refrigerant gas into core. RML lists in parallel with mirror shareholding, taking ~Rs.220 crores net assets and its own debt, free to raise its own capital and scale fleet toward profitability. Management expects sharper focus, clear capital allocation, value discovery.
rationale.gaps: No mobility valuation, EBITDA, debt quantum or record/listing date; no reason lender NOCs lagged; no explanation why wind stays with RIL or mobility's standalone funding needs.

rationale.rationale: Management presents the split as a deliberate strategic step, not housekeeping: on 14 February 2026 the Boards of Religare Enterprises (REL) and Religare Finvest (RFL) approved demerging the group's financial services businesses from its insurance business into two focused, independently listed entities, with REL's lending, broking and ancillary support services moving into RFL on a going-concern basis while the investment in Care Health Insurance stays in REL, leaving REL a pure-play health insurance holding company; REL shareholders get 1 RFL share for every 1 REL share, and RFL (today unlisted, an RBI middle-layer NBFC) is to list in Q1 FY2028. The stated rationale rests on four pillars: (1) streamlined business focus and a simplified structure, giving each side its own business model, growth strategy, capital deployment and performance metrics; (2) unlocking shareholder value through RFL's separate listing, which management says will enhance investor participation, facilitate targeted capital raising for the lending/broking business and allow more efficient allocation of management resources; (3) focused management attention and talent alignment, with dedicated leadership teams per entity so decision-making becomes faster, execution more focused and market response nimbler — explicitly tied to the senior hires under way (Group General Counsel Babu Rao from Bajaj Finance, Group CHRO Indranil Choudhury from UTI Mutual Fund, plus business leaders being identified); and (4) enhanced risk management and compliance, with risk policies and internal compliance frameworks tailored to each segment rather than one blended set. The enabling trigger management cites is the change of control — 'the takeover of REL by Burman Gr[oup]' — alongside strong promoter commitment: subscription to 50% of the preferential/rights issue with an INR750 crore commitment, open-market buying lifting promoter holding to ~30.3% (29.75% fully diluted on warrant conversion against 70.25% public), and an INR1,500 crore raise at REL level earmarked INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking and ~INR375 crore for general corporate purposes. The problem being solved is a holding company in which an insurer and a cleaned-up but sub-scale lending/broking stack sat together, confusing shareholders, diluting management focus and blocking segment-specific capital raising — against a backdrop of loss-making units (a subsidiary at an INR8.87 crore H1 FY26 loss versus INR6.63 crore in H1 FY25, and an INR5.93 crore loss in Q3 FY26 on revenue of INR7.11 crore versus INR7.79 crore) and badly under-levered lenders (NBFC net worth ~INR800 crore, HFC ~INR200 crore in Nov 2025; RFL later cited at INR900–1,000 crore net worth with ~INR600 crore cash and needing no fresh capital). Management also ties the demerger directly to scale ambitions: 'Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.' Mechanically it is a scheme of arrangement under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act 2013 needing regulatory, shareholder and creditor approvals, expected to run 15–18 months from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY28, with no change to REL's or RFL's existing regulatory registrations and, management insists, no operational disruption, no customer impact and no break in employee continuity.
rationale.evolution: On the Nov 2025 call the only demerger actually done was a small one — Religare Broking's e-governance business (a ~56,500-strong distributed-agent network for PAN/TAN/eTDS and bill-payment services) moved into wholly-owned Religare Digital Solutions under an NCLT-approved scheme — while investors did the pushing: Vikas Shrivastav asked what the corporate structure would look like in two years and specifically about 'the demerger of Care and the other two, three subsidiaries from the HoldCo', and Dixit Doshi asked whether value unlocking would come via a Care Health IPO or a demerger; management answered only with leadership hiring and the cleaning up of RFL's legacy issues. By the Feb 2026 call the plan was formal — boards approved it on 14 Feb 2026, and management laid out the four-pillar rationale, the 1:1 share entitlement, the retention of Care in REL and the 15–18 month path to a Q1 FY28 RFL listing. On the May 13, 2026 call the structure was unchanged but shareholder attention had moved past it: Sarvesh Gupta (Maximal Capital) and Vikas Srivastava (RBC) pressed on the holding company discount created by Care remaining a subsidiary of a listed REL and on a reverse merger of Care (noting the 19%-to-26% look-through gap and creeping-acquisition limits), with Arjun Lamba saying Kedaara remains a committed long-term partner, that separating FS from insurance was 'number one', and that the reverse-merger idea would be evaluated and answered later. By the time of the NSE observation letter (July 7, 2026) the scheme had cleared exchange no-objection under Regulation 37 and moved toward NCLT filing.

points.point: Pillars three and four: dedicated leadership teams per entity to make decision-making faster and market response nimbler (and to give clear mandates to the senior leaders being hired), plus risk and compliance frameworks tailored to each segment.
points.quote: The demerger enables implementation of spec ific risk management policies and internal compliance frameworks tailored to ea

points.point: Mechanics: REL's lending, broking and ancillary support services go to RFL on a going-concern basis with Care retained in REL; RFL issues shares 1:1 to REL shareholders and then lists, with Religare Broking as its direct subsidiary and Religare Housing Finance as a fellow subsidiary in affordable housing.
points.quote: The lending, broking and ancillary support services held under REL shall be demer ged into RFL on a going concern basis. The investment in CARE shall continue to be retained in REL.

points.point: Process and timeline: a Sections 230–232 scheme requiring regulatory, shareholder and creditor approvals, taking 15–18 months to a Q1 FY28 completion, with no change to existing regulatory registrations and no disruption to operations, customers or employees.
points.quote: The company expects the entire process to take 15 to 18 months starting from the current quarter and shall culminate in the first quarter of FY ‘28.

points.point: Management restated the end-state — RFL as an integrated financial services platform, REL as a pure-play health insurance holding company via Care — alongside promoter commitment of INR750 crore (50% of the preferential/rights issue) and a stake lifted to ~30.3% through open-market purchases.
points.quote: Under the proposed demerger, REL's lending, broking and ancillary financial services business will move to RFL, while REL will become a pure play health insurance holding company through its stake in Care Health Insurance business.

points.point: Shareholders pushed back that the chosen structure leaves Care as a subsidiary of a listed REL and therefore creates a holding company discount, repeating a concern first raised on the prior call and asking for a reverse merger of Care.
points.quote: So I think in the last call also, there were concerns raised regarding this demerger process and the hold ing company discount, which can be created because of this sort of a structure.

points.point: Arjun Lamba, for the promoters, acknowledged the investor concern but ranked clean separation of FS from insurance as the first priority, saying the reverse-merger question would be evaluated at an appropriate stage given how complex and regulator-dependent such restructurings are.
points.quote: And for us, number one has been to separate the FS business from the insurance business and to provide a clean structure so that the shareholders can understand, th e management can be very focused in doing what they have to do.

points.point: The separation is tied to a capital plan: of INR1,500 crore raised at REL, INR600 crore goes to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking and ~INR375 crore to general corporate purposes, while RFL (INR900–1,000 crore net worth, ~INR600 crore cash) needs none — all in service of scaling each business.
points.quote: Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.

points.point: The filing text supplied is NSE's July 7, 2026 Regulation 37 observation letter, not a rationale narrative: it conveys 'No objection' to filing the scheme with NCLT and requires REL to disclose the need for and rationale of the demerger, synergies, valuation and swap-ratio basis, segment financials, risks and RBI approvals to shareholders — i.e. the substantive rationale is still owed to shareholders, not stated here.
points.quote:
Need for demerger, rationale of the scheme, synergies of  business of the entities involved in 
the scheme, impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the s cheme.

points.point: Listing of RFL is conditional, not automatic — it is at the Exchange's discretion and subject to SEBI approval, an Information Memorandum, newspaper advertisement, frozen shares until trading permission, no change in RFL's shareholding or control between record date and listing, and trading starting within 60 days of the NCLT order.
points.quote:
However, the listing of shares of Religare Finvest Limited  
is at the discretion of the Exchange.

rationale.what_management_expects: RFL: an integrated, independently listed financial services platform with its own leadership, risk framework, targeted capital raising and faster decisions, scaling an under-levered NBFC (INR900–1,000 crore net worth, ~INR600 crore cash), housing finance and broking. REL: a pure-play health insurance holdco around Care, growing 24%-plus with INR600 crore infusion. Both: unlocked shareholder value, clearer structure, wider investor participation, no operational or employee disruption.
rationale.gaps: No swap-ratio or valuation basis, no fix for the Care holding-company discount or reverse merger, truncated Burman-takeover driver, no demerged-segment financials, RBI approval detail, or cost-benefit numbers.

rationale.rationale: Management says IGL is being split because its three businesses — the chemicals/green-chemistry business (retained in India Glycols), the Liquor plus Bio-Fuel business (going to IGL Spirits), and the herbal/biopharma business plus the small Bio Polymers (guar gum) business carved out of chemicals (going to Ennature Bio Pharma) — have, in Rupark Sarswat's words, "slightly different priorities, different markets, different drivers," and so should be run and grown independently. The board approved the scheme on 4 February 2025 along with the merger of promoter holding company Kashipur Holdings Limited into IGL, which is intended so that "the promoters will have the direct shareholding of IGL in their names." Anand Singhal sized the three entities on 9MFY25 numbers: India Glycols (chemicals) Rs. 1,079 crores turnover at 13.6% EBITDA margin; IGL Spirits (liquor + biofuel) Rs. 1,628 crores net turnover at 14.4%; Ennature Bio Pharma (biopharma + biopolymer) Rs. 178 crores at 14.9%. The stated benefits are four: independent growth for each business, reduced risk of one business affecting the others, potential value unlock "by drawing focused investors," and clear focus leading to improved management and resource allocation. Mechanically it is an NCLT-route demerger effective 1 April 2026 with all three companies to be listed, requiring SEBI, lender and NCLT approvals over a 12–15 month timeline, and the consortium lead State Bank of India is being engaged on splitting working capital and term debt. The debt split was progressively disclosed: Rs. 1,200 crores long-term debt in May 2025 (Rs. 500 crores chemicals / Rs. 700 crores liquor), then Rs. 1,400 crores in November 2025 split Rs. 600 crores India Glycols / Rs. 800 crores IGL Spirits, against which a Rs. 467 crores raise plus Rs. 180 crores of scheduled repayment was being applied. The demerger has also become the gating item for capital allocation and credit: capex is deferred until after it, and the credit rating sits on watch list with no upgrade possible until completion. Spirits was shown as the higher-return leg (ROCE of 17–18% per May 2025), while an investor challenged the logic of demerging Ennature given its margin collapse, which management conceded as a "margin squeeze" rather than degrowth.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced fully formed on the Feb 2025 call, where Sarswat opened with "the initiation of the scheme, which proposes to restructure IGL into three de-merged identities" following the 4 February 2025 board approval, with Singhal giving segment P&Ls, the Kashipur Holdings merger, the 1 April 2026 effective date and a 12–15 month approval runway. Through May 2025, Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 the discussion shifted from rationale to plumbing — allocating long-term debt between the entities (Rs. 500/700 crores, later Rs. 600/800 crores), deferring all large capex until after the split, and defending Ennature's economics against an investor who called its margins trading-like. By Feb 2026 the demerger had become a constraint as well as a plan: the credit rating was frozen on watch list until completion and capex explicitly postponed, and by the Jun 2026 call (transcript dated 18 May 2026) attention was on the NCLT second-motion hearing of 21 May 2026 and hopes of an order in the first ten days of June, after which ROC filing would follow.

judge.selling_pressure_why: Tiny entitlement (122 shares per 2,000 held) creates small odd-lot positions in a differently-focused EPC/evacuation business newly listed on BSE and NSE.

rationale.rationale: Inox Green Energy Services (IGESL) is hiving off its Power Evacuation / substation, connectivity and common-infrastructure business into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, the renamed Resco Global, which already runs the evacuation and EPC business), so that IGESL becomes a pure-play, zero-capex, annuity wind/solar O&M company and IRSL consolidates all evacuation plus EPC into one entity. The scheme's stated logic is that O&M and power evacuation have separate and distinct risks, rewards, financial profiles, competition and opportunities, and that the evacuation business can attract a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders, so consolidating it in IRSL unlocks value and gives each business independent focus; the scheme ends in two listed entities, one O&M and one EPC+evacuation. Management's central operating argument is accounting distortion: roughly INR1,000 crores of gross block sits on IGESL's balance sheet for substations on which it is, in Devansh Jain's words, only a trustee — already paid for by customers — and that block drags about INR50-55 crores of annual depreciation that masks true profitability, so EBITDA has had to be used as a proxy for PAT. Removing it makes the balance sheet 'cleaner and asset light', eliminates the depreciation, raises PBT by that amount (PBT becomes roughly equal to EBITDA and to cash profit, against FY27 EBITDA guidance of upwards of INR600 crores), and significantly improves ROE and ROCE, while only INR4-5 crores (later described as about INR10 crores) of revenue leaves and interest cost is unaffected. The transfer could not be done earlier because moving the historical substations would have required consent from over 200 O&M customers, who management said would have used it to renegotiate contracts and damage the O&M business; all new substations and transmission lines are already being built under Resco, so there is no future evacuation capex in IGESL. Shareholders also get paper: IGESL shareholders receive IRSL shares (management cited broadly 20% of Resco) with automatic listing of IRSL, which had raised INR175 crores at about a INR7,400 crores valuation, and the INR700 odd crores of accumulated tax losses stay with IGESL because they sit at company level, not asset level. The pressure came mainly from analysts and investors who could not isolate O&M EBITDA (Jatin Chawla, Nov 2023) and who repeatedly asked what the demerger does to revenue, depreciation, tax losses and value unlocking; debenture holders representing 100% in value voted unanimously in favour, and shareholders and creditors approved before NCLT sanction.
rationale.evolution: The seed appears in the [Nov 2023] call, where management could not show clean O&M EBITDA because traded-goods margins of INR7-8 crores, IPO charges and the fact that the entity 'had not been demerged from the EPC perspective' were mixed in. By [Aug 2024] the board had appointed consultants and registered valuers for the demerger of the power evacuation business, with a 6-9 month timeline, consequential listing of Resco, and the trustee/200-customer explanation of why it had not happened earlier; [Nov 2024] repeated that status verbatim. In [Feb 2025] the scheme was drafted with BSE/NSE approvals expected in early February and NCLT taking a further 6-9 months, Resco renamed Inox Renewable Solutions, and sizing added (20% of Resco to IGESL holders, INR700 crores tax losses retained); by [Sep 2025] exchange no-objections were in and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad with the INR1,000 crores gross block / INR50-55 crores depreciation framing, [Nov 2025] added shareholder and creditor approval and recast IRSL as Inox Wind's EPC arm, [Feb 2026] had it in final NCLT hearings, and [Jun 2026] reported NCLT approval with the depreciation already eliminated and IRSL listing pending administrative approvals.

points.point: Analysts could not extract O&M EBITDA because traded-goods margins (INR7-8 crores, under related-party compliance), one-time charges and IPO expenses were mixed in, and because the entity had not been separated from the EPC side — the earliest signal of the structural muddle the demerger later fixes.
points.quote: Plus, there were various other charges given that this entity had not been demerged from the EPC perspective plus the charges for the IPO.

points.point: Management admitted the disclosed segment numbers could not be unpicked by investors and offered a separate call with the finance team on one-time and IPO items.
points.quote: No, you won't be able to find that out because we could not apportion the profit margin on the traded goods in that.

points.point: The board formally appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate the demerger of the power evacuation business from Inox Green, with initiation subject to valuation reports and board approval.
points.quote: The board of Inox Green has appointed consultants and registered valuers for evaluating the demerger of power evacuation business from Inox Green.

points.point: The stated benefit was a cleaner, asset-light balance sheet plus value added through elimination of depreciation.
points.quote: Demerger of power infrastructure facilities currently on the balance sheet of Inox Green will result in a cleaner and asset light balance sheet.

points.point: Devansh Jain gave a 6-9 month timeline from board approval and said the outcome would be the consequential listing of Resco carrying Inox Green's power evacuation infrastructure.
points.quote: And post evaluation of reports and subject to the Board approval, the demerger would take place, which would lead to consequential listing of Resco, along with the power evacuation infrastructure of Inox Green.

points.point: The core problem: Inox Green is only a trustee of historical substations already paid for by customers, and they could not be moved to Resco earlier without consent from over 200 O&M customers who would have renegotiated contracts; all new evacuation assets are already built under Resco.
points.quote: We could not shunt it out from this balance sheet into Resco because that would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business.

points.point: Management framed residual Inox Green as a zero-capex annuity O&M business with no land banks and no future power evacuation, its balance sheet 'unnecessarily inflated' by the legacy substations.
points.quote: Inox Green's balance sheet is unnecessarily inflated thanks to these historical substations which are lying on its balance sheet of which we are actually the trustee.

points.point: Answering investor Bhavya Shah, CFO Manish Garg quantified the P&L impact: no interest-cost effect and only about INR4-5 crores of annual revenue leaving with the demerged assets.
points.quote: So Bhavya, to be very precise, there would be no impact on the interest cost as such, but a little bit of the revenue will go away, which is a very miniscule number.

points.point: Status repeated unchanged a quarter later — valuers and consultants appointed, process to start after valuation reports and board approval, with the same asset-light and depreciation-elimination rationale.
points.quote: The demerger of power infra facilities currently on the balance sheet of INOX Green will result in a cleaner and asset -light balance sheet.

points.point: Akhil Jindal told investors to treat EBITDA as the benchmark for PAT because the heavy depreciation now in Inox Green's numbers will transfer to Resco with the assets — an explicit admission that reported profit understates the business.
points.quote: There is a significant amount of depreciation charges that is being reflected in our current numbers, which would be transferred to Resco as assets get transferred.

points.point: Process detail: BSE/NSE approvals expected in the first week to 15 days of February, then NCLT taking another 6-9 months, with hopes of completion within calendar 2025 and Resco renamed Inox Renewable Solutions Limited being listed.
points.quote: Once the regulatory approval comes in, the demerger will be done through NCLT and that would take, say, another 6 to 9 months as the case may be.

points.point: Answering investor Deepak Sharma, S.K. Mathusudhana said Inox Green shareholders benefit twice — they receive Resco shares (he cited broadly 10%, then broadly 20% of Resco) and the full depreciation disappears so EBITDA converts to PBT and PAT.
points.quote: Secondly, after this merger, demerger will get completed, the complete depreciation will be go away from the financial numbers, and our EBITDA would be as Mr. Akhil has said will translate to PAT and P BT.

points.point: Asked by analyst Akhilesh whether the demerger removes accumulated tax losses, management confirmed the INR700 odd crores of losses sit at company level, not asset level, and stay with Inox Green.
points.quote: So the tax losses would be on a company level, not on an asset level.

points.point: Scheme received no-objection from the stock exchanges and was filed at NCLT Ahmedabad; management sized the effect as roughly INR1,000 crores of gross block off the balance sheet and INR50-55 crores of annual depreciation eliminated, lifting PBT and improving ROE and ROCE, with approval expected in 2-3 quarters.
points.quote: Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crores will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated , thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.

points.point: IRSL's standalone value was already being established: INR175 crores raised at roughly INR7,400 crores valuation, with EPC, blade and transformer manufacturing housed there and margin guidance raised to 18-19% for FY26.
points.quote: We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.

points.point: Investor Hansal Thakkar pushed further, asking whether IGESL and IRSL would eventually be demerged into the hands of Inox Wind shareholders; Akhil Jindal restated that the scheme covers only the substation, connectivity and common infrastructure, with automatic listing of Resco giving Inox Green holders its shares.
points.quote: As I mentioned to you last time, the attempt was to de -merge the substation business and the connectivity and common infrastructure from INOX Green into Inox Resco.

points.point: Shareholders and creditors approved the scheme; management framed it as value-accretive for both parents — IRSL listing as Inox Wind's EPC arm, Inox Green losing the depreciation on the demerged asset blocks.
points.quote: This will add value for both Inox Wind, with subsequent listing of Inox Renewable solution as an EPC arm of Inox Wind, and Inox Green with elimination of depreciation on demergers of the asset blocks

points.point: Scheme in final stages of hearing at NCLT Ahmedabad; management reiterated INR1,000 crores gross block and INR50-55 crores depreciation elimination, expecting NCLT approval in about a month and listing 1 to 1.5 months after, i.e. roughly 2-3 months in all, while refusing to commit to dates.
points.quote: Finally, I would like to inform our investors that the scheme of demerger of substation business from Inox Green and its subsequent merger into Inox Renewable Solutions is in the final stages of hearing at Hon ’ble NCLT Ahmedabad.

points.point: With zero depreciation post demerger and virtually nil finance cost, management confirmed to analyst Utkarsh Somaiya that PBT equals EBITDA and equals cash profit on FY27 EBITDA of upwards of INR600 crores, with a 25% deferred tax book entry (accounting PAT ~INR450 crores) but no cash tax outgo because of the tax shield.
points.quote: So, our PBT would be equivalent to EBITDA.

points.point: Revenue leakage was re-quantified for investor Prit Nagersheth as only about INR10 crores leaving against roughly INR50 crores of depreciation — no material impact on the earnings math.
points.quote: So post the demerger, as we have clarified on the multiple cores, there would be a very limited amount of revenue in the range of INR 10 odd crore will get out of the balance sheet.

points.point: NCLT Ahmedabad sanctioned the scheme; the INR1,000 crores gross block and INR50-55 crores of annual depreciation have been eliminated, ROE and ROCE have improved, and IRSL will be automatically listed once remaining approvals are received (Devansh Jain put completion at 1-2 months of administrative process).
points.quote: With this gross block of approximately INR1,000 crores has been elimin ated from Inox Green's balance sheet.

points.point: Asked by investor Pradeep Motwani whether it unlocks value for minority shareholders, Devansh Jain cast both separations as the group's value-creation engine, pointing to Inox Green's own spin-off as precedent amid complaints about recent share-price destruction.
points.quote: We've spun off Inox Green, which has created tremendous value.

points.point: Rationale (a): the two verticals — WTG O&M services and the Power Evacuation Business — both have growth and profitability potential but separate and distinct risks, rewards, financial profile, competition and opportunities, and evacuation can attract a different investor, partner and lender base.
points.quote: The nature of rislcs, rewards, financial profile, competition and opportunities are separate and distinct for the O&M services business and the Power Evacuation Business.

points.point: Rationale (a) continued: the evacuation business is explicitly said to appeal to a different set of capital providers and strategic partners than the O&M business.
points.quote: Further, the Power Evacuation Business is capable of attracting different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: Rationale (b): IRSL already undertakes the Power Evacuation Business, so the arrangement consolidates the same line of business in one entity, unlocking value and lending enhanced focus.
points.quote: The proposed arrangement would enable ccnsolidation of same line of business into IRSL, which uiill result in unlocking value for the Power EvacuatiorL business.

points.point: Rationale (c): the explicit objective is to make IGESL a pure-play O&M player by hiving off power evacuation.
points.quote: The Demerger aims to establish IGESL as a pure-play O&M player, and as a result, is considering hiving off the %wer Evacuation Business:

points.point: Rationale (d): the end state is two listed entities — O&M in one, EPC plus power evacuation in the other — each free to pursue its own strategy with independent focus for higher stakeholder growth.
points.quote: This will enable both the entities pursue their respective strategies to deliver higher growth for all stakeholders with specific independent focus on the respective businesses.

points.point: Creditor support was unanimous: debenture holders representing 100% in value of outstanding debentures (1,25,29,45,205 debentures) voted in favour, with none against.
points.quote: As per the Scrutinizer's Report, all the debenture holders who participated in the voting process voted in favour of the resolution approving the proposed Scheme and none voted against the same.

points.point: Regulatory friction, not strategic objection: the Regional Director asked for clarification of the accounting treatment of excess/deficit of net assets under Clause 8.1(b), goodwill treatment under Clause 8.2(g), FEMA/RBI compliance for foreign holders, Section 61 compliance for IRSL's authorised capital increase, and exchange-compliance undertakings; ROC reported no pending inquiry or prosecution.
points.quote: It is submitted that upon examination of the Scheme, the Regional Director has observed that the accounting treatment in respect of excess or deficit of net assets of the demerged undertaking, as referred to in Clause 8.l(b) of the Scheme, has not been clearly specified and therefore the Petitioner Companies may be directed to clarify the accounting treatment to be adopted in accordance with the applicable Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS).

rationale.rationale: Management frames the demerger as a strategic refocusing: Piccadily wants to be a global alco-bev company, so on the April 29, 2026 call (tagged May 2026) it announced that, with management and Board approval granted the prior day, it had filed a scheme of demerger of the sugar business into a new entity, with KPMG as advisor on the exercise and the scheme filed with SEBI; the next steps are SEBI go-ahead then NCLT, with completion envisaged by FY'27. The stated intent is to 'pool our human and capital resources just for the Alco-Bev business' and focus only on the Alco-Bev brand portfolio, while sugar — described as a 'traditional heritage business' — is separated and listed as its own entity rather than sold (management did not say sale was the plan when asked). The backdrop is an alco-bev business carrying the group: FY26 consolidated PBT up 79% from INR35 crores to INR63 crores on premiumisation (Indri, Cashmir Vodka), standalone revenue up 33% from INR270 crores to INR364 crores, standalone PBT up 17% to INR63 crores and PAT up 14% from INR40 crores to INR46 crores, with the distillery/Alco-Bev business growing 42% in FY26; FY27 is expected to be 'exceptional' at 60%–70% growth, helped by the Indri plant adding INR250–300 crores and the 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh greenfield adding INR300–400 crores, with 3x–4x revenue in 3–4 years and a Scotland malt distillery in the works (land, licences and approvals in place, construction starting). The scheme filing quantifies the demerged sugar division at 20.53% of the listed entity's FY26 turnover and sets a 1-for-9 share entitlement ratio (one PFEL share of INR10 for every nine PAIL shares of INR10), fixed on the sugar undertaking's turnover and assets, with no cash consideration and no change in PAIL's shareholding pattern. The filing's rationale is that separating the businesses lets each give 'focused attention for growth of their core businesses and attract required investments', brings greater business focus and shareholder value, unlocks value through price discovery of the individual entities, creates the right operating architecture with sharper individual strategies and 'clear capital allocation', and lets two separately listed companies attract their own specific investor sets and achieve financial flexibility. Resulting company Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited (PFEL) is currently a wholly owned subsidiary whose pre-scheme capital will be cancelled, and its new shares will be listed on BSE and NSE; the stock exchanges issued No Adverse Observation Letters dated August 14, 2026, intimated August 17, 2026.
rationale.evolution: The supplied material contains only one call — April 29, 2026 (tagged May 2026) — so the idea cannot be traced across the three years claimed; on that call management said only that 'we've been discussing this' before Board approval on April 28, 2026, giving no earlier dated discussion. Within that call it appears three times: first as a formal announcement of the filed scheme with SEBI/KPMG and an FY'27 completion target, then restated in the growth outlook as a demerger 'just to focus on the main Alco-Bev business', and finally in Q&A, where analyst Himanshu Shah asked whether the sugar business would be sold or separately listed and management clarified the intent is separate listing and pooling resources into Alco-Bev, not a sale. The only later step evidenced is procedural: BSE and NSE No Adverse Observation Letters dated August 14, 2026, intimated to the exchanges on August 17, 2026.

rationale.rationale: Thomas Cook (India) Ltd. (TCIL) is carving out its Resorts and Resort Management Business and demerging it into Sterling Holiday Resorts Ltd. (SHRL), its wholly owned hospitality subsidiary, which will then be listed separately on BSE and NSE. The Board's stated logic is a split by industry dynamics: TCIL is a travel company (Travel Services and Financial Services/foreign exchange) that happens to own and operate resorts across India — including curated segments like Adventure Holidays (trekking, kayaking, rafting, zip lining), Educational trips (survival skills, self-defence, nature appreciation) and Corporate Getaways (team building, wellness, leadership) — while SHRL already has deep experience running hotels for a different demographic, so TCIL and SHRL's Boards believe the resort assets 'would reap more benefits on account of expertise of SHRL in similar kind of business.' SHRL's Board separately says SHRL has 'matured over the years' and is 'well poised to chart its own growth path' as a standalone listed company in the fast-growing hospitality industry. The demerged undertaking is small in TCIL's revenue terms — INR 70 crore of turnover for the year ended 31 December 2025, about 0.4% of standalone turnover — so the move is about focus, structure and value rather than size: management (Mahesh Iyer) said the restructuring lets TCIL 'streamline our capital structure and concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business,' and that the scheme will 'unlock value for our shareholders.' The demerger rides inside a composite scheme that also (a) merges three dormant, non-operative wholly owned subsidiaries — TC Visa Services (India), Jardin Travel Solutions and Borderless Travel Services — which are 'incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs,' and (b) consolidates TCIL's face value 4 Re-1 shares into 1 Rs-4 share, followed by a reduction of face value from Rs 4 to Rs 3 with no payment to shareholders; management said the face-value consolidation plus the dormant-subsidiary merger 'further simplifies our corporate structure and improves our Earnings Per Share.' The scheme says the consolidation should improve key financial ratios so the share price better reflects intrinsic value and conveys 'stronger financial stability and valuation metrics.' No cash changes hands: TCIL shareholders get 81 SHRL shares of Rs 10 each for every 100 TCIL shares of Re 1 each, leaving SHRL at an indicative 65.55% promoter (including 7% retained by TCIL), 2.16% ESOP trust and 32.30% public, with 65,70,000 ESOP 2024 options accelerated; TCIL's own shareholding pattern is unchanged. Timing context matters: FY26 consolidated income rose 3% to INR 83,982 million but EBT fell 14% to INR 3,268 million on the Middle East geopolitical crisis (hitting Desert Adventures, the Middle East destination management unit, and DEI, with ~50% of revenue from UAE), while TCIL sits on roughly INR 16 billion (INR 1,600 crore) of forex float against INR 277 crore debt, i.e. ~INR 730-740 crore net cash.
rationale.evolution: The idea first surfaced from the sell side, not management: on the May 2024 call Dhaval Desai asked whether Sterling's margin profile would hold and whether 'at any point in time in future, would we think of demerging Sterling and listing it separately' — Vikram Lalvani answered only the margin half (hospitality margins run 30-35%, Sterling is already there and should stay at 34-36%) and the passage shows no commitment on the demerger. Nothing further appears until March 2026, when the Board granted in-principle approval for the demerger of the resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts, announced as a 'strategic divestment.' By the May 2026 call it had become live execution: Mahesh Iyer framed it as capital-structure streamlining and value unlock, Vikram Lalvani confirmed 'the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated' alongside Sterling's own brand re-architecture over the next 2-4 quarters, and after Ananya Khanna (Alpha Alternatives) asked for timeline clarity, Debasis Nandy said the Board-approved 12-15 month plan is on track, applications are filed with NSE and BSE with queries being answered, and completion is still expected by Q1 FY28 — the original guided timeline.

rationale.rationale: No earnings-call passages were supplied — the "CALL PASSAGES" section arrived empty — so the reasoning below comes solely from the scheme filing and the July 24, 2026 NCLT-convened meeting notice. The transaction is a demerger of the Textile Business Division of Kitex Childrenswear Limited (KCL, the Demerged Company) into Kitex Garments Limited (KGL, the Resulting Company, listed as KITEX), under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013, Section 2(19AA) of the IT Act and the SEBI Scheme Circular. The filing's stated objective is "consolidation of Textile business division of KCL in KGL for better growth so that Kitex Childrenswear Limited can concentrate on its other core activities." The operational trigger given is the existing arrangement in which KCL's textile work was done "as job work with final revenue booked in KGL," while "Considering the huge demand for capacity, KCL has decided to use its full capacity for its own revenue" — i.e. the job-work-into-KGL structure was no longer workable once KCL needed its own capacity. The filing says KCL houses two verticals, Textile Business Division and Remaining Business, whose "nature of risks, returns, growth and competition... are distinct and requires attribution of dissimilar technical and managerial focus"; the textile division employs around 4,900 people and spends on CSR above the statutory limit. The claimed benefits are focused growth, operational efficiencies, business synergies and increased customer focus for textiles; economies of scale and a "common pool of production" by combining similar activities under one entity (KGL being "engaged in the similar business and a pioneer in the said field"); the ability of each business to attract a "different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders"; insulation and de-risking of the two businesses from one another; and value unlocking through "better price discovery of individual platforms," explicitly to "open-up windows to unlock value through potential divestments and acquisitions." Consideration is new KGL equity shares issued to KCL's shareholders of record on a proportionate basis per the Share Entitlement Ratio, with the undertaking transferring on a going-concern basis at book values, liabilities included. Procedurally, the NCLT Kochi Bench ordered meetings on January 22, 2026 (CA(CAA)/01/KOB/2026), and shareholder and unsecured-creditor meetings were held by video conference on July 24, 2026, with remote e-voting from July 20 to July 23, 2026.
rationale.evolution: The evolution cannot be reconstructed: no earnings-call passages were provided in the prompt, so there are no call dates, no first mention of the idea, and no record of how the structure or perimeter changed over time. The only datable steps visible in the supplied documents are the NCLT Kochi order dated January 22, 2026 directing the meetings, and the equity-shareholder (11:00 A.M.) and unsecured-creditor (2:30 P.M.) meetings held July 24, 2026 after e-voting that ran July 20–23, 2026. At that meeting no shareholder registered to ask a question, so the Q&A was dispensed with and only a chat box was offered — meaning even the meeting record adds no management commentary on rationale.

rationale.rationale: The supplied texts do not contain management's stated reasoning — the only document provided is the NSE observation letter (Ref: NSE/LIST/52937, May 15, 2026) and the opening of the BSE letter (DCS/AMAL/RD/R37/73/2026-27), both procedural, and the 'CALL PASSAGES' section of the prompt is empty. What the filing does establish is structure, not motive: this is a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013 between Lloyds Realty Developers Limited ('Transferor Company 1'), Indrajit Properties Private Limited ('Transferor Company 2'), Lloyds Enterprises Limited ('LEL' or 'Transferee Company') and Lloyds Realty Limited ('Resulting Company'), filed under Regulation 37 of SEBI LODR read with the SEBI Master Circular of June 20, 2023. So two private/unlisted entities are absorbed into listed LEL while a resulting company, Lloyds Realty Limited, is created and taken to listing — implying a realty business is being carved out of LEL into a separately listed vehicle, with shares allotted to LEL shareholders per a share exchange ratio. The exchange explicitly left the rationale to be supplied by the company later, directing LEL to put before shareholders the 'Need for the merger/demerger, rationale of the scheme and swap ratio, synergies of business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the minority shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the scheme,' plus the valuation report, growth-rate justification, and three years of Revenue, PAT and EBITDA for every entity. Lenders feature only as a consent gate, not as requesters: NOCs are required from lending scheduled commercial banks/financial institutions/debenture trustees per para A(2)(k) of Part-I of the SEBI Master Circular, and any 'Conditions imposed by lenders' must be disclosed with their impact on the scheme. SEBI's own comment of May 15, 2026 requires disclosure of all ongoing adjudication, recovery and enforcement proceedings against the company, its promoters and directors before the NCLT and shareholders. No numbers, margins, segment figures, investor requests or partner demands appear anywhere in the provided text, so any specific rationale would have to be invented — which I will not do.
rationale.evolution: No earnings-call passages were supplied — the 'CALL PASSAGES:' heading in the prompt is followed by nothing, so there is no call-by-call record to trace and no call dates to cite. The only dated evidence is regulatory and terminal rather than formative: the NSE observation letter and SEBI's comments, both dated May 15, 2026, with the no-objection valid for six months from that date within which the scheme must be filed with the NCLT. By that point the structure was already fixed in the draft scheme, and NSE barred further change — 'no changes to the draft scheme except those mandated by the regulators/ authorities / tribunals shall be made without specific written consent of SEBI' — so nothing in these texts shows how or when the idea surfaced or how it was revised.
