rationale.rationale: Maharashtra Seamless Limited (MSL) is splitting into three listed entities: a composite scheme approved by the Board on 07 October 2026 (appointed date 01 October 2026) demerges Demerged Undertaking 1 into MSL Seamless Tubes Limited (MSTL) and Demerged Undertaking 2 into United Seamless Limited (USL), both currently wholly owned subsidiaries whose ₹1,00,000-share pre-scheme capital is cancelled and reissued to MSL shareholders. On FY2025-26 operational turnover, DU1 is ₹793 crore (16.98%), DU2 ₹693 crore (14.84%) and the remainder staying with MSL ₹3,185 crore (68.18%) of ₹4,671 crore total. The Board's stated reason is that MSL runs multiple undertakings with distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies, customer bases, logistics, capital requirements and growth trajectories — specifically three manufacturing plants on three different technology platforms (CPE at Nagothane, MPM at Mangaon, FQM at Telangana) serving different industry segments, plus a drilling/rig business and renewable power assets. The scheme says manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have different capital intensity and funding needs, so separation permits better assessment of capital needs, focused deployment and flexibility for expansion; renewable assets move with the undertaking they power, for energy-management efficiency and sustainability support. The rig business is called out as having distinct operational and commercial characteristics versus pipe manufacturing, warranting focused management and operational planning. The Board also expects improved transparency through independent financial and operational reporting, better performance evaluation and long-term value creation. It is structured to be value-neutral — 1 share of each resulting company (INR 5) for every 5 MSL shares (INR 5), keeping the same proportionate holding (promoters 70.3008%, public 29.6992%), with no cash consideration, no creditor compromise and listing of MSTL and USL on BSE and NSE. The trigger on the calls was investor pressure on what MSL would do with the rig and its surplus cash.
rationale.evolution: The idea first surfaces on the Nov 2023 call as a rig disposal, not a demerger: analyst Vikash Singh asks whether the plan to sell the single rig has been dropped given strong oil prices and cash flows, and D.P. Jindal says it has not been dropped but they are 'looking for the right time to hive off', adding they already have a plan for ₹852 crore of cash and want investors to benefit from it. By the Nov 2024 call the option set has widened and acquired a date — analyst Rishabh describes it as a plan to 'demerge or sell' the rig business post May 2025 — but Kaushal Bengani declines to give any realisation expectation because the matter had not yet reached the Board. By the scheme filing of 07 October 2026 the plan has changed shape entirely: no sale, and far wider scope than the rig — a two-way demerger of whole operational undertakings (manufacturing plants on different technology platforms, drilling and renewable power assets) into two separately listed companies, with the rig segregation now only one of seven stated benefits.

points.point: An analyst asks whether the long-stated plan to sell MSL's single rig has been abandoned given good oil prices and strong free cash flow; the Chairman says the plan stands but is waiting on timing.
points.quote: No, we have not dropped, but we are looking for the right time to hive off.

points.point: Pressed on what MSL would do with surplus cash it has no avenues to deploy, D.P. Jindal cites an existing plan for ₹852 crore, openness to opportunities in the same line of business, and a commitment that investors benefit from the cash.
points.quote: First, we have a plan for these 852 crores, and then we are also open for any new opportunity in the same field of business.

points.point: An analyst frames the rig plan as demerger-or-sale with a post-May 2025 timeline, asking what realisation and how long the process takes — showing the demerger route was already in investors' understanding two years before the scheme.
points.quote: Also on the rig business that you have, I understand that you are planning to demerge or sell it post May '25.

points.point: Kaushal Bengani refuses any valuation or realisation figure, saying the rig separation is an intention not yet taken to the Board, and that communication will follow Board approval.
points.quote: We don't have an expectation figure right now because that matter has not yet been discussed at Board level.

points.point: Capex discussion is confined to the ongoing Telangana debottlenecking and what is already in the presentation; no restructuring or separate-capital-pool argument is offered on the call.
points.quote: We have that. That is why we are doing the debottlenecking at Telangana.

points.point: The Board's threshold finding is that MSL houses several undertakings that differ on nearly every operating dimension, justifying reorganisation into separate focused companies with identical proportionate shareholding.
points.quote: The said undertakings having distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration, commercial considerations and growth opportunities.

points.point: Benefit (a): the three manufacturing sites — Nagothane, Mangaon and Telangana — serve different industry segments and are to become independent verticals with dedicated management.
points.quote: The manufacturing undertakings at Nagothane, Mangaon and Telangana cater to different industry segments and operate with distinct product portfolios, customer profiles and market dynamics.

points.point: Benefit (b): the plants run three different pipe-making technologies, each needing its own specialised management, modernisation path and technical expertise.
points.quote: The manufacturing facilities operate on different technological platforms, including CPE technology at Nagothane, MPM technology at Mangaon and FQM technology at Telangana, each requiring specialized operational management, modernization initiatives and technical expertise.

points.point: Benefit (d) — the capital-allocation argument: pipe manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have unlike capital intensity and funding profiles, so separation sharpens assessment of capital needs and expansion flexibility.
points.quote: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses have different capital intensity and funding requirements.

points.point: Benefit (e): renewable power assets are not pooled centrally but ride along with the undertaking they serve, for energy-management efficiency and sustainability support.
points.quote: The renewable power assets proposed to be transferred along with the respective undertakings are expected to provide better operational alignment, energy management efficiencies and support sustainability initiatives of the corresponding businesses.

points.point: Benefit (f) carries forward the rig question raised on both calls, now as segregation rather than sale, justified by the rig business being commercially unlike pipe making.
points.quote: The rig business has distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business.

points.point: Benefit (g): independent reporting for each entity is expected to improve transparency and performance evaluation and create long-term value — the closest the filing comes to a valuation-rerating argument.
points.quote: The proposed demerger would result in creation of focused business entities with independent financial and operational reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, improving performance evaluation and facilitating long-term value creation for stakeholders.

points.point: Scale of what leaves MSL: DU1 ₹793 crore (16.98%) and DU2 ₹693 crore (14.84%) of FY2025-26 operational turnover, against ₹3,185 crore (68.18%) retained, on a ₹4,671 crore total.
points.quote: Demerged Undertaking 1 793 16.98% Demerged Undertaking 2 693 14.84% Remaining 3185 68.18% Total 4671 100.00%

points.point: Consideration is paper, not cash: a 1-for-5 share entitlement in each resulting company, expressly engineered to leave shareholder economics unchanged (promoters 70.3008%, public 29.6992% in both MSTL and USL).
points.quote: The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.

points.point: Both resulting companies are to be listed, making this a three-way listed split rather than an internal reorganisation; creditors are untouched, with no compromise offered and liabilities following their undertakings.
points.quote: The equity shares of MSTL and USL shall be listed and admitted to trading on BSE and NSE pursuant to the Scheme subject to receipt of requisite approvals from statutory and regulatory authorities.

rationale.what_management_expects: Three focused, separately listed entities: each undertaking pursuing an independent growth strategy with dedicated management, technology-specific operational focus and strategies tailored to its end-user sectors; operational efficiencies and optimum resource utilisation; better assessment of capital needs, focused deployment and expansion flexibility across manufacturing, drilling and renewables; renewable assets aligned to the businesses they power; independent reporting improving transparency, performance evaluation and long-term stakeholder value. Value-neutral to shareholders.
rationale.gaps: No margin, EBITDA, valuation or rerating figures; no asset-to-undertaking mapping; no mention of lenders, partners, investor demands for demerger, timelines, costs, or why sale became demerger.

rationale.rationale: The filing is not a classic value-unlocking spin-off: Thermax is pulling businesses INTO the listed parent and leaving only a residual activity outside. Two linked steps sit in one Scheme of Arrangement and Amalgamation. (1) Amalgamation: a wholly-owned subsidiary engaged in 'setting up Energy Projects, Energy Exchange Platform and providing Energy Services including provision of electrostatic precipitators, regenerative air preheaters and related services' — a shell-sized entity with Rs 10.0 cr paid-up capital, Rs 0.6 cr net worth and Rs 0.8 cr total income as on March 31, 2026 — is merged into Thermax Ltd. (net worth Rs 4,427.09 cr, total income Rs 6,518.2 cr) to 'simplify overall group structure and reduce administrative overheads,' with management claiming 'a significant improvement in certain key financial ratios,' annual group cost savings, and 'stronger financial stability and valuation metrics' that present 'a more accurate picture of the Company's financial strength.' (2) Demerger: the Technology/EPC undertaking of Thermax Bioenergy Solutions Private Limited (incorporated August 12, 2022; CIN U40107PN2022PTC213848; WOS), covering Engineering, Procurement and Construction scope for Bio-CNG projects, is carved out and transferred into Thermax Ltd. because it is 'in line with the business of the Company' — turnover Rs 239.35 cr, or 3.67% of Thermax's FY26 revenue. The stated problem it solves is focus and vertical segregation: once EPC leaves, Bioenergy Solutions is meant to concentrate on its remaining O&M segment, while each entity 'pursue[s] growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics.' Notably, Bioenergy Solutions carries negative net worth of Rs (106.9) cr against Rs 38.0 cr paid-up capital and Rs 260.9 cr total income, which the rationale text never addresses. Both steps are cashless and cosmetically neutral to owners: all transferor/demerged shares are already held by Thermax and its nominees, the transferor's shares 'stand cancelled,' no new shares are issued, and there is no change in the shareholding pattern; Bioenergy Solutions stays an unlisted wholly-owned subsidiary.
rationale.evolution: No earnings-call passages were supplied — the 'CALL PASSAGES:' section of the prompt was empty, so no call-by-call development of the idea can be traced and no call dates exist in the source. The only datable evidence is the scheme filing itself, dated against financials as on March 31, 2026, alongside unaudited standalone and consolidated results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Within the filing, the sequencing is logical rather than chronological: Annexure A sets out the amalgamation of the energy-projects/energy-exchange subsidiary, and Annexure B the demerger of the Bio-CNG EPC undertaking into the same listed entity.

points.point: Step one is an upstream amalgamation of a wholly-owned energy subsidiary — energy projects, an energy exchange platform, electrostatic precipitators and regenerative air preheaters — into listed Thermax Ltd.
points.quote: business of setting up Energy Projects, Energy Exchange Platform and providing Energy Services including provision of electrostatic precipitators, regenerative air preheaters and related services etc.

points.point: The merger rationale is structural simplification, lower administrative overhead and better financial ratios, not operational separation.
points.quote: In order to simplify overall group structure and reduce administrative overheads, Management has proposed consolidation of Transferor Company with the Company which is expected to result in a significant improvement in certain key financial ratios.

points.point: Management also claims recurring group-level cost savings and long-term shareholder value from the merger.
points.quote: The proposed merger is also expected to result in annual cost savings for the Thermax Group, thereby enhancing long- term shareholder value

points.point: A valuation/perception argument is made explicitly: consolidating resources is meant to signal financial stability and better represent Thermax's balance-sheet strength.
points.quote: Such consolidation of resources is also anticipated to convey stronger financial stability and valuation metrics, thereby presenting a more accurate picture of the Company's financial strength and long -term prospects.

points.point: Step two demerges the EPC undertaking of Thermax Bioenergy Solutions Private Limited — the Technology, Engineering, Procurement and Construction scope for Bio-CNG projects — into Thermax Ltd.
points.quote: The Scheme of Arrangement and Amalgamation provides for demerger of EPC business undertaking of the Demerged Company which is involved in business of Technology, Engineering, Procurement and Construction scope for Bio-Compressed Natural Gas (Bio CNG) projects.

points.point: The EPC carve-out is justified as consolidating like with like, since the demerged activity duplicates the parent's own business.
points.quote: The demerged undertaking business is in line with the business of the Company and thus the management has decided to consolidate the similar businesses by demerging the EPC segment into the Company.

points.point: What is left behind at Bioenergy Solutions is the O&M business, which management says can now be the entity's focus.
points.quote: The management of Demerged Company believes that the demerger of EPC will help them focus on the remaining segment O&M, wherein they can undertake various operation and maintenance services for projects.

points.point: The broader objective is stated as segregating business verticals so each entity follows its own industry dynamics, improving efficiency and profitability.
points.quote: The main objective of the proposed restructuring, by way of a scheme, is to re- organiz e and segregate the different business verticals and focus on core businesses, in compliance with relevant regulations.

points.point: Each entity is expected to chase differently-shaped growth, with margin and efficiency gains cited as the payoff.
points.quote: In this manner, the two entities can each pursue growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics, leading to improved operational efficiencies and profitability.

points.point: The demerged EPC undertaking is sized at Rs 239.35 crore of revenue, a modest 3.67% of Thermax's FY26 consolidated turnover.
points.quote: The turnover of demerged undertaking as on March 31, 2026 was Rs. 239.35 Crores which consti tutes 3.67% of total turnover of Resulting Company in the immediately preceding financial year / based on financials of last financial year (year ended March 31, 2026).

points.point: Both legs are intra-group and cashless — no shares issued, no consideration, and the transferor's shares held by Thermax are simply cancelled.
points.quote: Further, the shares of the Transferor Company held by the Transferee Company directly, shall stand cancelled with out any further act/instrument or deed.

points.point: Public shareholders are unaffected on paper: there is no change in Thermax's shareholding pattern from either step.
points.quote: There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company pursuant to the Scheme, as no shares are being issued by the Transferee Company in connection with the Scheme.

points.point: No separate listing results — Bioenergy Solutions stays an unlisted wholly-owned subsidiary holding only O&M, so there is no demerger-listing value event for investors.
points.quote: Further, the Demerged Company is a wholly- owned subsidiary of the Resulting Company. Accordingly, upon the proposed Scheme coming into effect, the Demerged Company shall continue as an unlisted company & will remain a wholly -owned subsidiary of the Resulting Company.

points.point: The financial exhibit shows why the EPC business is being absorbed upward: Bioenergy Solutions has negative net worth of Rs (106.9) cr on Rs 38.0 cr paid-up capital and Rs 260.9 cr total income, against Thermax's Rs 4,427.09 cr net worth; the transferor is a near-dormant Rs 0.8 cr-income entity.

For Thermax Bioenergy Solutions: an undivided focus on O&M services, with each entity chasing growth suited to its own industry dynamics, yielding better operational efficiency and profitability.

rationale.rationale: On the texts supplied, the separation is not JSW Energy carving out one of its own businesses: it is GE Power India Limited (GEPIL) demerging its boiler manufacturing business into JSW Energy Limited (JSWEL), with GEPIL as Transferor/Demerged Company and JSWEL as Transferee/Resulting Company under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act 2013. The only rationale management actually gives is on the October 2025 call, and it is an acquisition/vertical-integration rationale rather than a separation-of-conglomerate rationale: "This acquisition significantly enhances our in -house capabilities wit h both technology and people which is very critical for equipment manufacturing and supports our thermal power expansion plan." It sits inside a stated growth ambition of "capacity of 30 GW and 40 GWh of energy storage," pursued "in a calibrated and strategic manner" to "ensure predictability in execution." It is explicitly one of a bundle of three same-quarter moves: the GEPIL boiler scheme, completion of a majority stake in KSK Water Infrastructure (which supplies raw water to the 1,800 MW KSK Mahanadi plant and is equipped for a further 1,800 MW), and a battery assembly plant in Pune. Management frames it alongside the SANY wind-turbine manufacturing partnership and the decision to pause its own solar module manufacturing plans — i.e. buying in equipment capability where a partner or an acquisition is available, and dropping in-house build where it is not. The scheme filing text provided contains no rationale section at all: it is BSE/NSE observation-letter language that merely *requires* the company to disclose "Need for the demerger, Rationale of the scheme and swap ratio, Synergies of business of the entities involved in the scheme." Consideration appears to be JSWEL shares to GEPIL shareholders, since the exchanges require a table of GEPIL shareholders, the share exchange ratio, and their "Classification in JSWEL post scheme."
rationale.evolution: Only one call passage was supplied, so no multi-call evolution is observable: on the Oct 2025 call the boiler-business scheme is announced as already signed, listed first of three strategic developments for the quarter, with no prior-call build-up in the provided text. The filing trail then runs NSE's reference letter to SEBI dated December 31, 2025, SEBI's comments dated March 30, 2026, and the NSE observation letter dated April 01, 2026, which gives JSW Energy six months to file the scheme with the NCLT. Nothing in the supplied texts shows the plan's terms changing between those dates; SEBI explicitly bars changes to the draft scheme after filing except those mandated by regulators.

points.point: The scheme is announced as an inbound acquisition of GE Power India's boiler manufacturing business via a Scheme of Arrangement, the first of three strategic developments for the quarter.
points.quote: We have entered into a Scheme of Arrangement with GE Power India Ltd. to acquire its boiler manufacturing business.

points.point: The stated reason is in-house equipment capability — technology and people — to support thermal expansion; this is the only rationale management gives anywhere in the supplied texts.
points.quote: This acquisition significantly enhances our in -house capabilities wit h both technology and people which is very critical for equipment manufacturing and supports our thermal power expansion plan.

points.point: The move is framed as part of a selective manufacturing strategy: partner with SANY for wind turbines, acquire boilers, and stop the in-house solar module plan.
points.quote: This approach aligns with our recent partnership wit h SANY for wind turbine manufacturing and our decision to pause our solar module manufacturing plans .

points.point: The growth frame cited is a 30 GW / 40 GWh storage ambition, to be pursued with execution predictability for all stakeholders.
points.quote: The opportunity for growth in this sector is immense, and we are committed to pursuing it in a calibrated and strategic manner .

points.point: A parallel vertical-integration step: completed majority stake in KSK Water Infrastructure, sized for 1,800 MW of existing and 1,800 MW of future thermal capacity.
points.quote: This entity currently supplies raw water to our 1,800 MW KSK Mahanadi Thermal Power Plant and is equipped to support an additional 1,800 MW, ensuring readiness for our future expansion.

points.point: The legal structure confirms the direction of the separation: GEPIL is the Demerged Company and JSW Energy the Resulting Company, under Sections 230-232.

rationale.rationale: Triveni is executing a Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Board on 10 December 2024 with two legs: the amalgamation of Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises (SSEL, a ~61.77%-owned subsidiary) into Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd (TEIL), and the demerger of the Power Transmission Business (PTB) undertaking of TEIL into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd (TPTL), a wholly owned subsidiary that will be separately listed. On the SSEL leg, the scheme says both companies have sugar and distillery manufacturing verticals, so merging them consolidates all sugar, alcohol and ethanol operations into one entity, creating 'operational synergies, economies of scale, optimum utilization of resources,' eliminating duplication, cutting administrative and multi-entity compliance costs (statutory filings, labour law/establishment compliances) and improving the combined entity's 'competitive position and negotiating power.' On the PTB leg, the filing argues PTB and the Residual Business 'address different market segments with unique opportunities and dynamics in terms of business strategy, customer set, geographic focus, competition, capabilities set, talent needs and distinct capital requirements,' so separation lets each sharpen focus, improve competitiveness, operational efficiency and agility; PTB has 'attained a significant size, scale and has a large headroom for growth' and is 'entering the next phase of growth,' which the Board says warrants focused management attention; and because PTB has 'separate growth trajectories, risk profile and capital requirement,' segregation enables 'independent value discovery' and unlocking of value for each business. Tarun Sawhney framed it on the Feb 2025 call purely as 'value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important,' and by Feb 2026 as being 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies.' The growth case was backed with capex: an incremental ₹60 crore approved in Feb 2025 on top of a ₹500 crore programme, taking gears capacity from ~₹400 crore today to ₹700 crore by September 2026, against a global high-speed and turbo gears market of only $650–700 million dominated by European gearbox makers, plus a Swiss subsidiary driving exports and qualification orders in oil and gas (pumps and compressors). Per the filing's FY2024-25 audited-accounts table, the demerger moves roughly ₹36,988.71 lakh of gross revenue and ₹13,693.93 lakh of EBITDA into TPTL (with a corresponding ₹36,689.32 lakh / ₹13,693.93 lakh reduction at TEIL), entitling TEIL shareholders to ONE ₹2 TPTL share for every THREE ₹1 TEIL shares, while SSEL holders get 100 TEIL shares for every 137 SSEL shares. The initiative was Board-driven, not demanded by lenders or partners; investors engaged mainly to contest the structure — Resham Jain of DSP Asset Managers argued the ~30% stake TEIL retains in TPTL means 'the same Holdco discount will be applicable,' to which Sawhney replied there were two reasons and that the Triveni Turbines precedent 'was actually quite a positive one for the Company.'
rationale.evolution: The scheme was announced on 10 December 2024 and first discussed with investors on the Feb 2025 call, where Sawhney laid out both legs, tied it to Board-led value unlocking, paired it with the ₹60 crore gears capex to ₹700 crore by September 2026, guided to NCLT approval 'by the end of this calendar year,' and defended the retained ~30% TPTL stake against Resham Jain's Holdco-discount objection. Through Jun 2025 and Aug 2025 the story became procedural and the timeline slipped — SEBI approval pending, then stock-exchange questions and 'another 30-odd days,' with completion pushed to Q1 of the next fiscal year, while investors asked for granular PTB disclosure ahead of separate listing and Sawhney began describing Board workshops on what the residual sugar/alcohol business does with its investable cash flows to regain 2022-23 margins. By Nov 2025 exchanges had approved and NCLT stakeholder meetings were set for end-November/early-December with culmination guided to Q4 FY26; the Feb 2026 call added the explicit purpose language 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies,' confirmed shareholder and creditor approval in December 2025, and reported systems work so TPTL could 'hit the ground' as a standalone. On the Jun 2026 call Sawhney confirmed the scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval, with appointed dates of 1 April 2025 (amalgamation) and 1 April 2026 (demerger), the SSEL record date of 3 June and the TEIL record date within four weeks, and CFO Suresh Taneja held PTB's ~35% PBIT as the go-forward trend.

points.point: First investor call after the 10 December 2024 Board approval; Sawhney framed the Composite Scheme entirely as Board-driven value unlocking, comprising the amalgamation of SSEL (TEIL owns ~61.77%) into TEIL and the vesting of the Power Transmission Business undertaking into wholly owned Triveni Power Transmission Ltd.

points.point: The growth case for a standalone PTB was backed by capex approved the previous day: an incremental ₹60 crore on top of a ₹500 crore project already underway, lifting gears capacity from approximately ₹400 crore today to ₹700 crore by September 2026.
points.quote: The Board meeting of the Directors concluded yesterday had an important announcement of an incremental capex of ₹60 crore for the enhancement of capacity in the Power Transmission business.

points.point: Sawhney said the ₹700 crore gears capacity had to be in place for business expansion the Board was evaluating, explicitly rejecting a 3-5 year payback horizon for the investment.
points.quote: We won't be investing so much money into a business that we're going to get 3-5 years from now.

points.quote: As far as the Scheme of Arrangement is concerned, we anticipate approval from NCLT by the end of this calendar year.

points.point: Resham Jain (DSP Asset Managers) attacked the structure, arguing that TEIL retaining ~30% of the demerged entity reimports the holding-company discount and replicates the earlier Triveni Turbines arrangement rather than achieving a clean separation.

points.point: Sawhney defended the retained stake with two reasons, the first being that the Triveni Turbines precedent had been good for the company — but the passage cuts off before the second reason is given.
points.quote: I think the experience with Triveni Turbines was actually quite a positive one for the Company.

points.point: The scheme was sitting with SEBI awaiting approval, with NCLT as the next step; Sawhney said the company was proceeding as per plan.
points.quote: With respect to the scheme of arrangement that is underway, I'd like to just briefly comment that this lies with SEBI at this particular point in time.

points.point: Resham Jain pressed that PTB's granular economics were poorly understood because it sat inside a much larger company, and asked for customer and industry-mix disclosure ahead of separate listing; Sawhney called it a welcome suggestion and agreed.
points.quote: And since it was a part of a much larger company, the understanding of this business from the very granular perspective was much lower.

points.point: Sawhney walked Udit Gupta through the remaining mechanics — SEBI approval, then NCLT with court-convened meetings, then automatic listing in four to eight weeks — while conceding the timelines were not fixed.
points.quote: Upon approval from NCLT, then it is an automatic listing process which takes another anywhere between four to eight -odd weeks, etc.

points.point: Still awaiting regulatory approvals, with continuous SEBI follow-ups and questions answered from the stock exchanges; Sawhney conceded roughly 30 days of slippage while holding to Q1 of the next fiscal year.
points.quote: If anything, it could add another 30 -odd days.

points.point: Asked by Rajesh Majumdar what the residual sugar/alcohol business does post-demerger beyond ethanol, Sawhney said Board workshops were planned to evaluate options, citing good investable cash flows and the need to recover the margin structure of 2022-23 — nothing concrete yet.
points.quote: And we have to do something to regain as well as the previous person mentioned the margin structures that we had in 2022-23.

points.point: Stock exchange approval was in hand and the process moved to NCLT, with stakeholder meetings for the two companies scheduled for end-November and early December and completion guided to Q4 of the fiscal year.
points.quote: The proposed scheme has been approved by the stock exchanges, and the process is obtaining approval of NCLT.

points.point: Sawhney stated the dual purpose explicitly for the first time on a call — unlocking value and driving operational efficiencies — and confirmed shareholder and creditor approval in December 2025 with a further NCLT hearing in February.
points.quote: Lastly, with respect to the proposed scheme of amalgamation of SSEL and the demerger of the Power Transmission business to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies, the scheme has been approved by shareholders of creditors, this was in December of 2025.

points.point: Ahead of separation, PTB was being equipped with standalone capability — skill sets and systems work so the new company could operate independently from day one.
points.quote: Looking at the Power Transmission business, gaining a lot of skill sets in terms of ability to operate as a separate company.

points.point: Sawhney opened the Q4 FY26 call — convened a few days late so all senior management could attend, and described as historic — by confirming the scheme effective from 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval, alongside FY26 revenue of ₹6,291 crore and PBT of ₹378 crore.

points.point: PTB's standalone growth drivers were exports led by the new Swiss subsidiary plus oil-and-gas qualification orders for pumps and compressors, with Q4 order booking 25% higher and a significant increase in enquiries, all pointed at TPTL's independent listing.

points.point: The amalgamation leg is justified as consolidating all sugar, alcohol and ethanol manufacturing into one entity because SSEL and TEIL have overlapping sugar and distillery verticals.

What is labelled 'SCHEME RATIONALE' is not a scheme document: it is (a) a 6 June 2026 Regulation 30 board-outcome filing recording that Mrs. Diksha Sharma stepped down as Company Secretary/Compliance Officer on health and maternity grounds and that Mr. Jayesh Patel was appointed from 7 June 2026, and (b) an 11 September 2026 press release announcing full exit from the NCLT/IBC resolution framework one year early. The only business facts available concern the NCLT exit: the ₹2,401 crore resolution-plan consideration (₹501 crore cash payable over five years to 30 September 2027, plus ₹1,900 crore 30-year bonds at a 0.001% coupon redeemable at an NPV of 16% per annum) prepaid in full in September 2026, availing lender pre-payment discounts; the acquiring consortium of Mr. Rakesh Shah, GSEC and the Monarch Group; clearance of all CBI and ED proceedings predating the IBC acquisition; and eligibility for credit ratings with the entire gross block (Vadodara plant, machinery, rod mills, captive power) freed for bank financing. None of this is framed as, or connected to, a separation of a business. No businesses proposed for separation are named, no demerged undertaking is identified, no swap ratio or record date appears, and no investor, lender or partner is cited as having asked for a separation. Answering the question as posed would require inventing content these texts do not contain.
rationale.evolution: No evolution can be traced: zero earnings-call passages were provided, so there are no call dates to anchor to. The only dated documents are the 6 June 2026 Company Secretary change filing and the 11 September 2026 NCLT-exit press release, neither of which mentions a separation at any stage. The single word in all the material touching restructuring is a line in the incoming Company Secretary's biography referring to prior experience with amalgamation/demerger schemes at other companies.

points.point: The document supplied as the scheme rationale is in fact a Regulation 30 board-outcome filing dated 6 June 2026 about a Company Secretary resignation and appointment; it contains no scheme of arrangement and no separation rationale.
points.quote: Noted that Mrs. Diksha Sharma, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, Key Managerial Personnel (ACS:56317) has step down from her said position with effect from close of business hours of June 6, 2026 with a view of health issues and availing maternity leave.

points.point: The only reference to demerger anywhere in the material is generic prior-employer experience in the incoming Company Secretary's profile — not a statement about any DICABS transaction.
points.quote: He possesses extensive experience in SEBI regulations, Companies Act compliances, corporate restructuring, amalgamation/demerger schemes and corporate governance matters.

points.point: The 11 September 2026 press release describes a full prepayment of the NCLT resolution-plan consideration, not a business separation: ₹501 crore cash plus ₹1,900 crore of 30-year bonds, ₹2,401 crore in total, settled a year before the 30 September 2027 deadline.
points.quote: The Company has prepaid, in full, the entire ₹501 crore cash Plus 30 years Bonds aggregating Rs 1900 cr consideration payable to its erstwhile lenders under the NCLT-approved Resolution Plan.

points.point: Strategic direction is stated as consolidation and scale-up within one entity — MV/EHV cable capacity, backward integration, customer expansion — with no mention of splitting or housing any business separately.
points.quote: The Company returned to sustained profitability in FY 2023-26, and its strategic focus now shifts wholly to scaling MV/EHV cable capacity, deepening backward integration, and expanding its customer base as India undertakes the largest grid build-out in its history & the company will not carry its NCLT Tag in large Projects.

points.point: Benefits claimed in the press release are attributed solely to exiting the resolution framework — rating eligibility, unencumbered gross block, no legacy CBI/ED overhang — and are not attributed to any separation of a business.
points.quote: With the Resolution Plan fully implemented and no obligation outstanding towards the erstwhile lenders, the Company is now eligible to obtain credit ratings from recognised rating agencies in the ordinary course — opening access to bank credit, the debt capital markets and institutional investors on standard commercial terms.

The only expectations expressed are for the single existing company post-NCLT exit: eligibility for credit ratings, access to bank and debt-capital-market funding, the entire gross block available as security, no legacy legal overhang, a debt-light balance sheet, and a growth phase scaling MV/EHV cable capacity.

rationale.rationale: These texts do not describe a separation, demerger or spin-off at all — they describe the opposite, a buy-in and full consolidation, so no separation rationale can be reconstructed from them. The only transaction explained is Eris Lifesciences' acquisition of the remaining 30% of Swiss Parenterals Limited (parenterals, incorporated 4 February 1997, presence in ~80+ countries) from Mr. Naishadh Shah, a Director of Swiss, taking Eris from 70% to 100% so that Swiss becomes a wholly owned subsidiary. The stated objects are 'fully consolidating its position, enhancing operational synergy, and strengthening its long-term strategic presence', with expected benefits of complete managerial control, full financial consolidation, improved cost efficiencies, streamlined governance and enhanced shareholder value. Consideration is INR 423.30 crore, discharged not in cash but by a preferential issue of up to 23,06,372 equity shares of face value Re. 1 at INR 1,835.35 each (premium INR 1,834.35), taking Mr. Shah from nil to 1.69% on a fully diluted basis, priced per Chapter V of the SEBI ICDR Regulations and a valuation report of 24 November 2025 by Rashmi Shah, Independent Registered Valuer (IBBI/RV/06/2018/10240). It is disclosed as a related party transaction (a transaction with a related party of a subsidiary under Regulation 2(zc) of SEBI LODR), stated to be at arm's length, with no promoter/promoter group/group company interest, no governmental or regulatory approvals required, and completion expected before 31 March 2026. The scale cited for Swiss is group-level turnover of INR 220.80 crore (FY2022-23), INR 282.97 crore (FY2023-24) and INR 351.11 crore (FY2024-25). No business is being carved out, no resulting entity is named, no demerger scheme or rationale clause is present, and no party (investor, lender or partner) is identified as having asked for anything.
rationale.evolution: No earnings call passages were supplied — the 'CALL PASSAGES' section is empty, so there is no call-by-call history to trace. The documentary trail runs only across two Regulation 30 intimations: the Board meeting of 24 November 2025 (2:45 PM to 5:30 PM) approving the 30% Swiss acquisition, the share-swap consideration and a postal ballot with a 21 November 2025 cut-off date; and the intimation of 16 January 2026 recording that shareholders approved by postal ballot on 24 December 2025 and that the Board's Executive Committee approved the allotment of the 23,06,372 shares that day. The plan therefore did not change over time in these texts — it moved from board approval to shareholder approval to allotment without alteration, and the filing explicitly records 'None' against any cancellation or termination of the issuance proposal.

points.point: The transaction is a consolidation, not a separation: Eris proposes to move from its existing 70% holding to 100% ownership of Swiss Parenterals, the stated purpose being consolidation of position, operational synergy and long-term strategic presence.
points.quote: With the objective of fully consolidating its position, enhancing operational synergy, and strengthening its long-term strategic presence, the Company now proposes to acquire 100% ownership of Swiss.

points.point: The benefits management lists are control, accounting and governance benefits rather than the focus/valuation arguments typical of a demerger rationale.
points.quote: This consolidation is expected to provide complete managerial control, enable full financial consolidation, improve cost efficiencies, streamline governance, and contribute to enhanced shareholder value.

points.quote: Pursuant to the said acquisition, Swiss will become a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

points.quote: The acquisition of 30% stake in Swiss by the Company from Mr. Naishadh Shah is proposed to be undertaken for a total purchase consideration of INR 423,30,00,000 (Indian Rupees Four Hundred and Twenty Three Crores and Thirty Lakhs Only), which will be discharged by the Company by way of issuance of up to 23,06,372 (twenty three lakh six thousand three hundred and seventy two) equity shares of the Company on a preferential basis to Mr. Naishadh Shah

points.point: The deal is flagged as a material related party transaction because Mr. Shah is a Director of the subsidiary Swiss, requiring postal ballot approval; it is asserted to be at arm's length with no promoter interest.
points.quote: The transaction is being undertaken at arms' length.

points.point: Swiss's cited scale and reach: parenterals sold in roughly 80-plus countries, with group-level turnover rising from INR 220.80 crore in FY2022-23 to INR 282.97 crore in FY2023-24 and INR 351.11 crore in FY2024-25; no regulatory approval is needed and closing is targeted before 31 March 2026.
points.quote: Country in which the acquired entity has presence : ~80+ countries

points.point: The second filing (16 January 2026) confirms execution: shareholder consent by postal ballot on 24 December 2025 and allotment of the full 23,06,372 shares at a premium of INR 1,834.35 approved by the Executive Committee of the Board.
points.quote: the Executive Committee of the Board of the Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e., January 16, 2026 has approved the allotment of 23,06,372 (Twenty-Three Lakh Six Thousand Three Hundred and Seventy-Two) fully paid-up equity shares of face value of Re. 1 (Indian Rupee One) each

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing is said about any separated entity, because none exists here. For Eris post-consolidation they expect complete managerial control, full financial consolidation of Swiss, improved cost efficiencies, streamlined governance, greater operational synergy, a stronger long-term strategic presence and enhanced shareholder value. No margin, capital-structure, leverage or valuation-multiple expectation is quantified, and no guidance is given on dilution impact from the 1.69% share issuance.

rationale.rationale: Per the scheme's own rationale, HEG Advanced Materials Ltd. (the First Petitioner / Demerged Company, CIN L23109MP1972PLC008290, incorporated 27 October 1972, registered office at Mandideep near Bhopal, Dist. Raisen, M.P.) says its two core businesses — manufacturing graphite electrodes (including other carbon products) and generation of thermal and hydel power — have each 'acquired critical mass' and now each need flexibility and independence to grow faster in a fast-changing, technology- and innovation-driven environment. The filing argues the two have differentiated strategies, different industry-specific risks, different market dynamics and different growth trajectories, and that the nature of competition in each is distinct, so each is capable of attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders; a structure 'amenable for future growth' is therefore required. The claimed benefits of segregation are unlocking value of each business for shareholders of the Demerged Company, better flexibility in accessing capital, separating businesses with different risk/return profiles so investors can choose what suits their strategy, focused growth strategy and focused management per business, greater visibility on each business's performance, enhanced operational efficiency, and de-risking the businesses from each other. Alongside the demerger into the Resulting Company (Second Petitioner, CIN U23994MP2024PLC071568, incorporated 4 June 2024, registered office c/o HEG Limited, NH-12, Mandideep), there is an amalgamation leg: the Transferee Company (the same First Petitioner) wants to consolidate the assets and liabilities of the Transferor Company (Third Petitioner) to streamline the corporate structure by consolidating multiple entities and gain efficiency through fewer legal and regulatory compliances and lower administrative costs. The amalgamation is further justified as establishing an 'independent brand identity of future oriented and new age business', combining resources to create synergies, optimally utilise resources, achieve greater economies of scale, and derive operating efficiencies from adopting the Transferor Company's existing technology-enabled processes. The filing concludes the Scheme is in the interests of all stakeholders of the Demerged/Transferee, Transferor and Resulting Companies. Important limitation: no earnings-call passages were supplied in this prompt — the 'CALL PASSAGES' section is empty — so no management commentary, operating or financial figures, segment margins, debt levels, capex, or named investor/lender/partner requests can be attributed, and none are present in the filing text provided (the only quantities given are share capital: authorised Rs 70,00,00,000 and paid-up Rs 38,59,58,810 across 19,29,77,530 equity shares of Rs 2 each for the First Petitioner, with 1,150 forfeited shares aggregating Rs 3,750; Rs 1,00,000 authorised and paid-up across 50,000 shares of Rs 2 each for the Resulting Company).
rationale.evolution: Cannot be reconstructed call by call: the prompt's 'CALL PASSAGES' section was delivered empty, so there are no tagged calls, no dates and no sequence of management statements to trace. The only chronology available is procedural, from the filing: a first-motion joint application CA(CAA) No. 01/MP/2026 was allowed by the NCLT Indore Bench by order dated 26 March 2026 (shareholder and creditor meetings directed for the First and Third Petitioners, dispensed with where there were no such classes or where consent affidavits existed); the second-motion Company Petition CP(CAA) 3 of 2026 was filed on 12 May 2026 and admitted on 14 May 2026, with the order in hand dated 13 August 2026. Whether the plan changed in scope, structure or timing is not shown by any text provided.

Each of the said businesses required flexibility and independence to grow faster in the fast-changing technology and innovation driven environment.

rationale.rationale: The stated primary object is to consolidate all NBFC business of the two applicant companies into a single entity. The trigger is regulatory: Sammaan Capital Ltd (SCL), the listed company, was formerly registered with the National Housing Bank as a non-deposit-taking HFC (certificate dated December 28, 2005, registration number 02.0063.05), a licence later surrendered; following a shareholder resolution of September 25, 2023 and an application to RBI for conversion from HFC to NBFC-ICC, SCL received a certificate of registration dated June 28, 2024, number N-14.03624, under Section 45IA of the RBI Act, 1934, and RBI directed while issuing it that no other group entity shall hold an NBFC-ICC/HFC CoR within a prescribed timeline. Because Sammaan Finserve Ltd (SFL) — a wholly owned subsidiary that is itself an NBFC-ICC and is the Demerged Company here, with SCL as the Resulting Company holding its entire equity — also holds such a licence, the demerger transfers SFL's NBFC business to SCL on a going-concern basis to comply. Management argues the merged lending book gets a wider and stronger capital and asset base, pooled resources, knowledge and client relationships, a more diversified product suite on a unified platform, simpler corporate structure, economies of scale, lower administrative and compliance cost and a stronger risk-management architecture. The split also frees SFL, which says it is contemplating entry into the strategically distinct insurance broking and insurtech business and wants a dedicated management and operational structure for it, citing sustained insurance-industry growth, rising dependence on the broking channel, digital disruption, favourable regulatory reform and rising investor interest. Mechanically it is structured as a tax-neutral demerger under Section 2(19AA) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, with no shares issued as consideration since SCL already owns SFL fully, and NCD holders of SFL receiving one NCD of SCL for every one held on identical coupon, tenure, ISIN, redemption price, quantum and security.

Nothing in the supplied text describes how management first raised the idea publicly or how it changed.

Prasad, which the texts never justify. The stated logic for the EPC split was that the two businesses were structurally unalike and were dragging on each other: five years before July 2024 the company was 'burdened with over 2,000 crores in debt' with 'numerous pending EPC orders', a period the Chairman called one 'of uncertainty and significant pressure', and the fix sequence was de-leveraging (debt-free as of March 2022) followed by the September 2023 demerger. Management's post-facto framing in the August 2024 call was that the demerger delivered 'data identity and focus for the 2 distinct businesses' and had shown up in market capitalization, i.e. the separation was pitched as identity, focus and re-rating rather than as a cash-raising or deleveraging event in itself. The cleanest problem it was said to solve was margin opacity in the consumer business: investors argued the EPC business inside BEL made 'the allocation of costs ... an issue', so a stand-alone consumer company would expose the true cost structure and be judged on its own margins. The pressure for clarity came from investors, not lenders or partners — Anuj Sehgal of Manas Asian Equities (Value Fund) pushed in both August and November 2024 that consumer durables had last done double-digit margins in FY12, twelve years earlier, sat at 'low single-digit margins' while smaller peers earned high single-digit to low double-digit EBIT, and asked whether there was a structural issue such as a bloated cost structure or distribution inefficiency. Management's answer (E.C. Prasad, November 2024) was that the double-digit margin guidance stays intact over the long term, that overheads already 'support a turnover of more than INR 6,000 crores' which current revenue does not fill, and that roughly 3-4% of margin would come from operating leverage as turnover returns. Supporting financial markers cited post-separation were Q1 FY25 cash from operations of Rs. 155 crores, surplus cash of Rs. 442 crores as on 30 June 2024, double-digit EBIT margins in the Lighting installations vertical, and a strategy of premiumization, digital transformation and cost competitiveness. The separation also required splitting shared legacy assets: the 1981 Employee Welfare Trust was bifurcated 67:33, described as the net worth ratio of Bajel and BEL at the time of the demerger, with trustees in the same ratio and the holding treated as jointly controlled.
rationale.evolution: In the July 2024 call the demerger is presented retrospectively, as part of Anuj Poddar's exit scorecard — debt-free by March 2022, EPC demerged in September 2023 into Bajel Projects Limited — rather than as a forward-looking plan. In August 2024 management upgraded the claim to a verdict: the demerger was 'a great success' in identity, focus and market capitalization, while the same call (and again in November 2024) saw investor Anuj Sehgal press that the removed cost-allocation excuse had not yet produced double-digit consumer margins, prompting Prasad's 'levers' answer about the INR 6,000 crore-capable cost base and 3-4% operating leverage. By May 2025 the story had moved to mechanics and clean-up — the Employee Welfare Trust finally split 67:33 on the demerger-date net worth ratio — and in the call reported for Nov 2025 (dated October 31, 2025) the frame widened from one demerger to a sequence, crediting the departing CFO with the EPC demerger plus a newly 'carved out' Lighting Solution vertical. The March 16, 2026 filing text supplied here adds nothing on rationale, mentioning the EPC demerger only as a line in an incoming interim CFO's profile.

points.point: Investor Anuj Sehgal (Manas Asian Equities Value Fund) applies the post-demerger test directly: consumer durables last earned double-digit margins in FY12, twelve years ago, and still runs below smaller peers — is the problem structural (bloated costs, distribution inefficiency)?

points.point: Mechanics of unwinding shared legacy assets: the 1981 Employee Welfare Trust, left undivided at the time of the demerger, was split 67:33 on what management called the Bajel/BEL net worth ratio at that date, with trustees in the same ratio, producing a jointly controlled JV line in the balance sheet.
points.quote: But now after that thing has settled down, we have decided that the trust would also be bifurcated in the ratio of 67% to 33%, which was the net worth ratio of the Bajel and BEL at that point in time.

points.point: The Chairman's farewell to CFO E.C. Prasad (joined November 2019, call dated October 31, 2025) widens the restructuring story from one demerger to a programme: EPC demerger, debt-free balance sheet, a carved-out Lighting Solution vertical and a streamlined business model — the only mention of the Lighting separation in these texts, with no rationale attached.

points.point: The filing text supplied is not a scheme rationale: it is the March 16, 2026 board outcome appointing Suketu Shah interim CFO and designating Rahul Pundir as senior management personnel. The EPC demerger appears only as a credential in Shah's profile, alongside a Rs 350 crore rights issue and 'evaluation of strategic investments and brand acquisitions' — no reasoning for any separation is given.

rationale.what_management_expects: Two distinct businesses each with its own identity and focus, with value recognised in market capitalization. For BEL: a debt-free, cash-surplus consumer and lighting company (Rs 442 crore surplus cash, Rs 155 crore quarterly operating cash), free of EPC cost-allocation distortion, reaching long-term double-digit margins as returning turnover fills a Rs 6,000 crore-capable cost base (3-4% from operating leverage), with Lighting installations already at double-digit EBIT.

rationale.rationale: Across these texts the "separation" is really one composite scheme with two legs: a demerger out of Wim Plast Limited (WPL) and the amalgamation of WimPlast into Cello World Limited (CWL), with Cello Consumer Products Private Limited (CCPPL) as the third party to the scheme — per the filing, WPL shareholders receive CWL equity "pursuant to the demerger and the amalgamation, in accordance with Clause 8.1 and Clause 16.1 of the Scheme, respectively." On the November 13, 2024 call, Gaurav Rathod gave exactly two rationales for folding WimPlast back in: first, "we do not see any point in running 2 separate listed entities as the business is not very different"; second, WimPlast's manufacturing footprint "in different parts of the country" can be shared with Cello's other plastic product lines. Management framed the standalone listing as the problem being solved — "standing outside was not making sense, and that's the reason that the merger is happening" — and explicitly ruled out any further break-up of Cello's three verticals, arguing furniture manufacturing "is very, very similar to our other plastic manufactured products." Housekeeping consequences management confirmed: WimPlast first becomes a 100% subsidiary of CWL, WimPlast's ~8% loan to Cello World is extinguished in the merger, and WimPlast shareholders get 86 CWL shares (per the analyst's restatement, which Rathod confirmed). The filing adds the mechanics: NCLT Ahmedabad sanctioned the scheme on May 14, 2026, the Board set May 27, 2026 as Effective Date with Appointed Date April 1, 2025 and June 09, 2026 as Record Date, and WPL's authorised capital combines into CWL's, reclassified to INR 140 crore (28 crore shares of INR 5). On the call tagged Jun 2026 (held May 29, 2026), management reported the scheme effective and FY26 comparatives restated from the beginning of the prior year, alongside FY26 revenue growth of 8.8%, EBITDA of INR526.4 crores (22.7% margin), PAT of INR331.5 crores (14.3% margin), CFO of INR255.1 crores, debt-to-equity of 0.01, capex of INR219 crores (steel bottle line, select consumerware, writing instruments, maintenance) and FY27 capex guidance of ~INR100 crores. No investor, lender or partner is named anywhere as having demanded the restructuring — the only pressure visible is analyst questioning, including Karan's observation that WimPlast traded at 10–12 PE against Cello World's ~60 PE, which management did not engage with as a rationale.
rationale.evolution: By the November 13, 2024 call the merger was already announced and management said it had "previously mentioned this as well," so the origin pre-dates these passages; that call is where the two rationales, the 100% subsidiary step, the 8% intercompany loan and the 86-share entitlement were spelled out under questioning from Deepesh Sancheti (Manya Financial Services) and Karan. Also in Nov 2024, management closed the door on the logical extension — demerging the three unrelated-looking verticals — on synergy grounds, so the direction of travel was consolidation, not separation. The plan then executes rather than changes: NCLT Ahmedabad sanctions it May 14, 2026, the Board declares it effective May 27, 2026 (Appointed Date April 1, 2025; Record Date June 09, 2026), and on the May 29, 2026 call (tagged Jun 2026) management reports completion plus restated comparatives and pending EPS impact. Nothing in these texts shows the rationale itself being revised, re-scoped or re-priced between 2024 and 2026.

rationale.rationale: This is not a carve-out of an existing Gabriel business but a composite scheme that moves promoter-held automotive assets into Gabriel: first the amalgamation of Anchemco India Private Limited into Asia Investment Private Limited (AIPL), then the demerger of AIPL's automotive undertaking into Gabriel India, bringing four promoter-held entities — Anchemco, Dana Anand, Henkel ANAND and ANAND CY Myutec (Dana Anand established 1993) — under the listed company. Management framed three rationales. First, product diversification: Gabriel moves "from a single product company into a diversified product company," with enhanced collaboration with its foreign strategic partners and synergies from economies of scale and shared resources, a wider customer base, supply-chain synergies, a larger product portfolio and a stronger aftermarket presence. Second, simplification of the group structure: consolidating AIPL's demerged automotive undertaking into Gabriel makes Gabriel "the growth engine for the automotive business," the group's vehicle for future growth against a group revenue target of INR50,000 crores by 2030. Third, it answers an explicit investor demand — management said it "addresses the repeated queries of investors on product diversification, M&A" by bringing existing mature JVs under the Gabriel fold. The financing argument was that Gabriel scales up "without any leverage or cash outlay," with roughly 40% EPS accretion on a current-scale basis and enhanced ability to raise funds for future organic and inorganic growth. Execution was made conditional on creditors, NCLT, stock exchanges, shareholders and majority-of-minority approval over a 10-12 month timeline; the NSE observation letter flags that promoter shareholding increases on implementation and tells investors to read all scheme documents before voting.
rationale.evolution: The transaction was announced at a dedicated call on 1 July 2025, where Chairperson Anjali Singh said the Board had approved the composite scheme and management walked through the slides, the four target entities, the two-step merger-then-demerger mechanics, the 40% EPS accretion and a 10-12 month approval timeline, noting the group had been "actively evaluating organic and inorganic opportunities" discussed in prior forums and calls. By the Feb 2026 call the discussion had shifted from rationale to process: NSE NOC received, application filed with NCLT, first-motion hearing in early January, scheme admitted and order pronounced by end-January, with management saying it was on the originally planned timeline. On the May 2026 call the scheme was reported as having received shareholder and NCLT approvals and becoming effective from 22 May 2026, and the conversation moved on to operating matters such as bringing Inalfa technology products to customers. The scheme filing text available (the 17 November 2025 NSE observation letter) contains only disclosure conditions, not management's rationale.

points.point: Chairperson Anjali Singh opened a transaction-only call saying the Board had approved a composite scheme of arrangement intended to realign the corporate structure, unlock synergies and sharpen competitiveness.
points.quote: This scheme of arrangement marks a meaningful step forward in realizing our group's strategic vision, realigning the corporate structure to unlock synergies and enhance our competitive edge.

points.point: Gabriel India is positioned as the group's growth vehicle and value-creation platform, against a stated group revenue ambition of INR50,000 crores by 2030.
points.quote: Gabriel India is set to play a pivotal role in this transformation, serving as our group's vehicle for future growth and the platform for long -term value creation.

points.point: Management identified four promoter-held businesses/investments to be acquired through the scheme, having been actively evaluating organic and inorganic opportunities.
points.quote: S o right now, we are looking at four entities An chemco, Dana Anand, Henkel ANAND and A NAND CY Myutec.

points.point: The mechanics are a two-step composite scheme — Anchemco merges into AIPL, followed by a demerger into Gabriel — subject to multiple approvals over 10-12 months.
points.quote: This is obviously subject to the key approvals from the creditors, NCLT, stock exchanges, shareholders, majority of minority and the time lines that we are looking at is 10 to 12 months subject to the regulatory approvals.

points.point: First rationale: diversification away from a single-product (shock absorber) profile, with deeper collaboration with foreign strategic partners and scale/shared-resource synergies, a wider customer base, supply-chain synergies and a bigger aftermarket presence.
points.quote: We are looking at enhanced collaboration with the foreign strategic partners and obviously, achieving synergies through economies of scale and shared resources.

points.point: Third rationale: group-structure simplification, consolidating AIPL's demerged automotive undertaking into Gabriel so Gabriel becomes the group's automotive growth engine.
points.quote: So this will consolidate the business of demerged undertaking of AIPL into automotive components making Gabriel the growth engine for the automotive business in the future.

points.point: Management said the scheme directly answers investors' repeated demands for product diversification and M&A, by bringing the group's existing mature JVs inside the listed company.
points.quote: And this also add resses the repeated queries of investors on product diversification, M&A by br inging the existing mature JVs under Gabriel fold.

points.point: The financial case: scale-up with no debt and no cash outflow, plus EPS accretion quantified at about 40% on a current-scale basis and improved fund-raising capacity.
points.quote: This helps Gabriel scale up without any leverage or cash outlay, accretion of EPS has been already explained by the Chairperson.

points.point: The quantified accretion and the funding benefit for future growth were stated together as 40% on the current scale.
points.quote: We are looking at a 40% on a current scale basis and the enhanced ability to raise the funds for future organic and inorganic growth.

points.point: Asked by Viraj Kacharia about quantified synergies, management offered only short-run examples, saying more would emerge as time unfolds; it also said overseas opportunities were explored but did not qualify.
points.quote: So I can give you a couple of examples, again of the synergies that we see in the, I would say, in the short run.

points.point: Mohit Srivastava gave a process update: stock exchange NOC received, NCLT application filed, first-motion hearing in early January and the scheme admitted with the order pronounced by end-January.
points.quote: So on the scheme of arrangement, we received the NOC from st ock exchange and post that, we filed our application to NCLT.

points.point: Management reaffirmed the original 10-12 month timeline was being met, answering Ananya Khanna's question on when statutory approvals would start rolling in.
points.quote: So we are very much on track what original time we had planned for this scheme and we've been p rogressing very well on this front.

points.point: Beyond the scheme, management described leaning on partner technology (Inalfa) to introduce newer-technology products with a different margin profile over the long term.
points.quote: There, definitely, I think Inalfa being very strong in technology, we are also trying to offer some newer technology products to customers.

points.point: The scheme cleared shareholders and NCLT, completing the Anchemco-into-AIPL amalgamation plus demerger of the automotive undertaking into Gabriel.
points.quote: So, I would like to update you all that the composite scheme involving the amalgamation of Anchemco India Private Limited into Asia Investment Private Limited followed by the demerger of automotive undertaking into Gabriel India has now received key shareholder and NCLT approvals.

points.point: An effective date was confirmed, alongside FY26 total dividend of INR5 per share versus INR4.7 in FY25.
points.quote: The scheme is becoming effective from 2 2 nd May 2026.

points.point: The NSE observation letter (17 November 2025) contains no management rationale text — only disclosure conditions, including that promoter/promoter group shareholding increases on implementation and that the impact on public shareholders' rights and value must be explained.
points.quote: Therefore, investors should read all the scheme related documents before exercising their voting rights.

points.point: NSE required the company itself to disclose the need for the merger and demerger, the rationale, the synergies, shareholder impact and a cost-benefit analysis — i.e. the rationale is referenced as a required disclosure, not supplied in this text.
points.quote: Need for the merger and demerger, Rationale of the scheme, Synergies of business of the entities involved in the scheme, Impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the scheme.

rationale.what_management_expects: Gabriel becomes a diversified multi-product automotive platform and the group's growth engine toward INR50,000 crores group revenue by 2030: about 40% EPS accretion on current scale, achieved with no leverage or cash outlay, deeper foreign-partner collaboration, wider customers, supply-chain and scale synergies, stronger aftermarket, simplified structure and better capacity to fund future organic and inorganic growth. Promoter shareholding rises.
rationale.gaps: No standalone revenue, margins or EBITDA for the four entities; no swap ratio, valuation basis or quantified synergies; no justification of the promoter stake increase; no AIPL residual-business detail.

rationale.rationale: The texts supplied do not contain any statement of why SKF India is separating the business — neither call passage nor filing gives a rationale, a strategic motive, or a requesting party. What they do establish is the mechanical fact pattern: SKF India Limited (the Demerged Company) demerged its industrial undertaking into SKF India (Industrial) Limited (the Resulting Company), incorporated 17 December 2024, under a Scheme of Arrangement between the two companies and their respective shareholders and creditors, sanctioned by the NCLT on 26 September 2025, with the Resulting Company's shares listed on the Main Board of BSE and NSE from 5 December 2025 and its CIN changed from U28140PN2024PLC236396 to L28140PN2024PLC236396. The separation created a standalone industrial entity whose history is not comparable: management reports quarter-on-quarter because year-on-year figures required extraction from SKF India Limited's books for 17 Dec 2024–31 Mar 2025 and 1 Apr 2025–30 Sep 2025 under Appendix C of Ind AS 103, with management assumptions. The only costs attributed to the separation are one-time: roughly INR 1.8 billion in Q3 FY26 (demerger IT costs, professional services and a large stamp duty on the land transfer from SKF India to SKF India (Industrial) Limited) and INR 183 million in Q4 FY26, mainly demerger-related IT. Q4 FY26 (Jan–Mar) sales were INR 9.5 billion, up 9.8% QoQ, with PBT of 9.5% — a 1,731 bps QoQ improvement — or 11.5% excluding one-offs versus 13.1% in Q3 on the same basis; net working capital fell 2.8% QoQ to 18.7% of sales. The standalone entity's FY mix was roughly 35% distribution, 51% OEM, 6% exports, 4% sales to SKF India and 3% other income, with OEM up 31% YoY (general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy 7%, railway 11%, metals 6%) — and management framed OEM as lower-margin business that builds long-term aftermarket. No problem to be solved, no investor, lender or partner request, and no valuation or capital-structure argument appears anywhere in these texts.

The earlier calls that would show how the idea surfaced and changed are absent from the material provided.

rationale.rationale: The supplied texts do not describe a separation/demerger of a business out of Aegis Logistics Ltd. (AEGISLOG, BSE 500003); they describe two intra-group transfers that consolidate storage/terminalling assets into the Group's terminalling vehicles. First, the scheme rationale section covers the transfer of an Ammonia storage terminal from Aegis Logistics Ltd. (ALL — described as engaged in developing, owning and operating a network of shore-based tank farm installations in India providing logistics solutions for oil, gas, chemicals and petrochemical industries) to ATPL, whose primary business is 'Storage, terminalling facilities of Oil, chemicals and petroleum products.' Management's stated reasoning is threefold: the Ammonia terminal strengthens the Group's position in specialized chemicals and gas logistics and supplies critical infrastructure for growing demand from the fertilizer, industrial and emerging clean-energy value chains; moving it to ATPL consolidates terminalling services under the Group and enables operational synergy; and it can create a new growth platform by leveraging Group expertise in sourcing, logistics and distribution while expanding into a strategically important product segment. The transfer is for cash consideration, is a related-party transaction done at arm's length, and causes no change in the listed company's shareholding pattern. Second, a Board intimation dated October 29, 2025 approves (subject to shareholder approval) the sale by wholly owned subsidiary Aegis Gas (LPG) Private Limited (AGPL) of 51% — 6,21,146 equity shares of INR 10 each — in Hindustan Aegis LPG Limited (HALPG) to associate company Aegis Vopak Terminal Limited (AVTL) for INR 7,01,60,71,920, after which HALPG ceases to be AGPL's subsidiary and the Company's step-down subsidiary; HALPG contributed FY25 turnover of INR 1,68,13,01,000 (2.49%) and net worth of INR 4,47,24,05,330 (10.07%), and completion is set for on or before January 15, 2026. rationale.rationale: On the evidence supplied, the separation is a holding-company clean-up of the GFL Group rather than an operating-business carve-out: a composite scheme of arrangement among Inox Leasing and Finance Limited (ILFL, the listed/NBFC holding vehicle), Inox Holdings and Investments Limited (IHIL) and Gujarat Fluorochemicals Limited (GFL/GFCL). Management's stated reason, given by Group CFO Akhil Jindal on the Dec 2024 call, is to 'make it a clean structure' so that ownership of GFCL passes directly into the hands of the ultimate shareholders, the promoters, and so that GFCL's holding company ends up 'just holding the GFCL assets rather than the combined' pool of unrelated assets it holds today. The mechanics in the filing match that: ILFL's demerged undertaking — explicitly including its mutual fund distribution activities and the brokerage income generated thereon (clarified by ILFL and IHIL board resolutions dated March 25, 2026) — goes to IHIL, ILFL's remaining assets and liabilities are transferred into GFL, and ILFL is to surrender its NBFC certificate, i.e. the financial-services and investment activities are stripped away from the fluorochemicals asset. A separate perimeter point was clarified on the same call: the existing Fluoropolymers business GFCL reports does not form part of GFCL EV (the EV/battery-materials entity), so fluoropolymers stays with GFCL. The investor-side motive was voiced by Ketan Gandhi of Gandhi Securities, who framed it as unlocking value 'after 20 years' for minority shareholders of the holding company and praised management for doing a demerger that 'takes care of their loyal shareholders'; management did not dispute that framing. Notably, no financial quantification was offered in any of the supplied text — management cited no revenue, EBITDA, capital, holding-company discount or value-unlock numbers. The scheme document supplied is in fact a BSE/NSE observation letter, in which 'the rationale and objectives underlying the proposed scheme' appears only as item (b) on a list of disclosures the exchanges require GFL to make, alongside a cost-benefit analysis, valuation/fairness-opinion details, promoter reclassification for GFL, and any lender-imposed conditions — so the company's own written rationale is requested there, not stated.
rationale.evolution: Only one call passage is supplied, Dec 2024, where the idea is already a live, announced plan: an analyst (Rohit Nagraj) asks a perimeter question confirming Fluoropolymers sits outside GFCL EV, a shareholder (Ketan Gandhi) thanks management for the holding-company restructuring and asks about the Wind business leg, and Akhil Jindal restates the goal as a clean structure with promoters owning GFCL directly.
