judge.what_is_spun: Purple Fabric, Intellect's Enterprise Intelligence Operating System / Business Impact AI platform, carved into an independent Line of Business
judge.reason: The intrinsic DNA of eMACH.ai and Purple Fabric are completely different; independent identity gives dedicated resources, freedom and agility to accelerate growth in the Business Impact AI market
judge.insiders: Deepak Dastrala appointed CEO/Business Head of Purple Fabric, reporting to Arun Jain, and becomes Intellect Management Council member and Senior Management Personnel; no shareholding stated
judge.hidden_value: A fast-scaling AI platform embedded inside Intellect: 45+ clients live, 95%+ accuracy SLA, 18-layer architecture, 550 domain-aware agents, described as a massive long-term value-creation opportunity
judge.selling_pressure_why: Internal Line-of-Business carve-out only; documents state no separate listing, share distribution or index change
judge.listing_timeline: not stated
judge.read_next: Purple Fabric segment revenue and profitability in the next quarterly results or segment disclosure
judge.quote: This carve-out provides the new LoB with the dedicated resources, freedom, and agility required to accelerate its growth journey and curate its own destiny in the Business Impact AI market.

listing.text: NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

rationale.rationale: Management frames the separation not as a financial restructuring but as an identity and speed problem: over the last two years Intellect curated two parallel architectural disruptions — eMACH.ai, its composable open-finance platform, and Purple Fabric, its Business Impact AI / Enterprise Intelligence Operating System — and concluded that the 'intrinsic DNA' of the two is 'completely different', so running them inside one structure was constraining both. The trigger cited is market timing: the enterprise AI market is at an inflection point, 'moving rapidly from AI experimentation to scaled, enterprise-wide deployment', which management says makes this the optimal moment to give Purple Fabric an independent identity. The stated problems the carve-out solves are shared/contested resources, lack of freedom and lack of agility; the carve-out gives the new Line of Business 'dedicated resources, freedom, and agility' to accelerate growth and 'curate its own destiny' in the Business Impact AI market. A second, explicitly cultural rationale is organizational design: Purple Fabric is to be an organization in 'flow' — young talent, boundaryless thinking, fluidity — abandoning traditional hierarchy for a networked 'Leadership Circle' model with micro-team, high-speed DNA, which management implies cannot be built inside Intellect's existing structure. Governance is set up accordingly: Deepak Dastrala becomes CEO and Business Head of Purple Fabric, reporting directly to Chairman and Managing Director Arun Jain, joining the Intellect Management Council as Senior Management Personnel, with Arun Jain continuing to mentor him and his leadership circle. The traction numbers offered as justification that Purple Fabric can stand alone are 45+ clients live, a 95%+ accuracy SLA for high-stakes financial workflows where minor errors have 'catastrophic consequences', an 18-layer architecture integrating hundreds of enterprise technologies, and 550 domain-aware agents for multi-agent orchestration. Arun Jain positions the two businesses as complementary rather than overlapping — eMACH.ai as 'foundational architecture', Purple Fabric as the 'critical cognitive intelligence' layer — and justifies the split by the scale of the prize, 'a massive long-term opportunity for value creation'. Note: no earnings call passages were supplied with this request, so the entire reconstruction rests on this single filing/announcement text.
rationale.evolution: No earnings call passages were included in the material provided, so no call-by-call evolution can be traced and no call dates are available. The only sequencing the text itself gives is retrospective: 'over the last two years' Intellect curated eMACH.ai and Purple Fabric in parallel, an effort Arun Jain calls 'a humongous effort', and only now — as the AI market shifts from experimentation to scaled deployment — has the company 'determined that it is the optimal time' to separate Purple Fabric. The structure announced is an independent Line of Business with its own CEO, not a described legal demerger, share-swap or listing, so whether the plan changed over time cannot be established from these texts.

points.point: The core stated reason is that the two platforms Intellect built in parallel over two years — eMACH.ai and Purple Fabric — have fundamentally incompatible business DNA, despite both reaching global customer adoption.
points.quote: Over the last two years, Intellect has successfully curated and nurtured two major, parallel architectural disruptions: eMACH.ai and Purple Fabric. While both represent historic milestones from concept to global customer adoption, the company acknowledges that the intrinsic DNA of eMACH.ai and Purple Fabric are completely different.

points.point: Timing is justified by an external market inflection — enterprises shifting from AI pilots to enterprise-wide deployment — which management says makes now the optimal moment to grant independence.
points.quote: As the market approaches an inflection point, moving rapidly from AI experimentation to scaled, enterprise-wide deployment, Intellect has determined that it is the optimal time to give Purple Fabric its independent identity.

points.point: The problems the separation is said to solve are resource competition, constrained freedom and slow agility; the fix is a dedicated resource pool and self-determination for the new LoB.
points.quote: This carve-out provides the new LoB with the dedicated resources, freedom, and agility required to accelerate its growth journey and curate its own destiny in the Business Impact AI market.

points.point: A distinct organizational-design rationale: Purple Fabric is to replace hierarchy with a networked 'Leadership Circle', micro-team model that would not fit Intellect's traditional structure.
points.quote: Moving away from traditional hierarchical structures, Purple Fabric will pioneer a networked "Leadership Circle" model where talent can wear multiple hats and roles, operating with a high-speed, micro-team DNA.

points.point: Governance of the carve-out: Deepak Dastrala is named CEO and Business Head of Purple Fabric, reporting directly to Arun Jain, and is elevated to the Intellect Management Council as Senior Management Personnel.
points.quote: In this role, Deepak will report directly to Arun Jain, Chairman and Managing Director of Intellect Design Arena, who will continue to mentor Deepak and his leadership circle.

points.point: The two businesses are positioned as complementary layers, not competitors — eMACH.ai as foundational architecture and Purple Fabric as the cognitive intelligence layer — with unique DNAs as the reason for independent status.
points.quote: "If eMACH.ai forms our foundational architecture, Purple Fabric provides the critical cognitive intelligence enterprises need to operationalize AI with complete confidence. Curating two major architectural disruptions in parallel over the last two years has been a humongous effort. However, because their intrinsic DNAs are entirely unique, granting Purple Fabric independent LoB status gives it the freedom and dedicated resources to accelerate its growth."

points.point: Scale evidence offered for standalone viability: 45+ live clients, a contractual 95%+ accuracy SLA, an 18-layer architecture spanning hundreds of enterprise technologies, and 550 domain-aware agents.
points.quote: ● 45+ Clients Live: Successfully operationalized across global enterprise environments. ● 95%+ Accuracy SLA: Bringing trusted reasoning and execution to zero-uncertainty workflows. ● 18-layer Architecture: Integrating hundreds of enterprise technologies into a unified framework. ● 550 Domain-aware Agents: Enabling advanced multi-agent orchestration and contextual reasoning.

points.point: Product justification: Purple Fabric targets high-stakes financial workflows where error tolerance is near zero, which management uses to explain the guaranteed accuracy SLA and the need for autonomous, governed execution.
points.quote: Purpose-built for high-stakes financial environments where minor errors hold catastrophic consequences, the platform guarantees a 95%+ accuracy SLA to ensure trusted, autonomous execution.

points.point: The new CEO frames independence as enabling maximum focus and a shift of the AI conversation from speculative tools to measurable business outcomes with full enterprise governance.
points.quote: "Backed by our proven 18-layer architecture and 550 domain-aware agents, our new independent structure allows us to scale with maximum focus and help global enterprises operationalize AI with total governance and control."

points.point: Residual Intellect is described as retaining a broad financial-technology franchise — eMACH.ai, iTurmeric, the 8012 Design Center, 500+ customers across 61 countries — across eight banking and insurance domains.
points.quote: Intellect serves over 500+ customers across 61 countries, supported by a global workforce of domain, solution and technology experts.

rationale.what_management_expects: For Purple Fabric: dedicated resources, freedom, agility, maximum focus, faster growth, a young non-hierarchical Leadership Circle culture, and capture of 'a massive long-term opportunity for value creation' in Business Impact AI. For Intellect/eMACH.ai: an undiluted foundational-architecture identity across its banking, wealth, insurance and capital-markets platforms. No margin, capital-allocation, funding or valuation-unlock expectations are quantified or even claimed in the text.
rationale.gaps: No earnings-call passages supplied. No financials, revenue, margins, capital or funding needs; no legal demerger structure, share entitlement, listing, timeline, or any investor, lender or partner demand for the split.

rationale.rationale: The materials supplied do not contain any statement of why Laurus Labs Ltd. is separating a business: the "CALL PASSAGES" section is empty (no earnings-call text was included), and the three documents filed under "SCHEME RATIONALE" are purely procedural Regulation 30 disclosure letters, not the scheme's rationale section, which is described as "truncated" and in fact contains none of it. What the documents do establish is the structure of the transaction: a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 among Laurus Synthesis Private Limited (LSPL, the Demerged/Transferor Company), Sriam Labs Private Limited (Sriam, the Resulting Company) — both wholly-owned subsidiaries of Laurus Labs — and Laurus Labs Limited (Transferee Company). The scheme has two legs: (i) the "Identified Business Undertaking," i.e. Unit-1 of LSPL, is demerged into Sriam Labs; and (ii) the "Remaining Business Undertakings" of LSPL (entire LSPL excluding Unit-1) are amalgamated into Laurus Labs Limited itself. Because both entities are already wholly-owned subsidiaries, this is an internal reorganisation of subsidiary assets rather than a listed-shareholder spin-off, and no share-entitlement ratio, valuation, financials or segment numbers appear in the texts. Procedurally, unsecured creditors of both LSPL and Sriam approved the scheme at NCLT-directed meetings held April 06, 2026 with requisite quorum; the NCLT Amravati Special Branch passed an order on July 24, 2026 directing service of Form CAA-3 notices on authorities, regulators and stakeholders, and set the petition hearing for September 10, 2026. No business reason, no cited metric, no named investor, lender or partner request, and no mention of margins, capital allocation or value unlocking appears anywhere in the supplied material. Any rationale beyond the structural facts above cannot be reconstructed from these texts, and I am not supplying one from memory.
rationale.evolution: Only the filing trail is visible, and it is procedural rather than substantive: the July 25, 2026 letter back-references prior scheme disclosures dated August 21, 2025 and September 05, 2025 (first disclosures), then February 24, 2026 (NCLT direction to convene unsecured-creditor meetings), then April 07, 2026 (creditors of both LSPL and Sriam approved the scheme at meetings held April 06, 2026). On July 25, 2026 the company disclosed the NCLT order pronounced July 24, 2026 directing CAA-3 notices and fixing September 10, 2026 as the next hearing; as of today no outcome of that hearing is in the supplied documents. A further letter dated October 6, 2026 concerns an unrelated INR 12,09,60,500 rights-issue investment in associate Kurnool Renewables Private Limited (holding unchanged at 26%), not the scheme. There are no earnings calls in the input, so no call-by-call evolution of the idea can be traced.

points.point: Leg one of the composite scheme: Unit-1 of Laurus Synthesis Private Limited, labelled the "Identified Business Undertaking," is demerged into Sriam Labs Private Limited, another wholly-owned Laurus subsidiary. No reason for carving out Unit-1 specifically is given.
points.quote: the demerger of Laurus Synthesis Private Limited (“LSPL” or “Transferor Company” or “Demerged Company”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Laurus Labs Limited, whereby the Identified Business Undertaking (i.e., Unit-1 of LSPL) shall be demerged into Sriam Labs Private Limited (“Sriam” or “Resulting Company”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Laurus Labs Limited

judge.insiders: not stated; mirror-image demerger means the Resulting Company's shareholding pattern mirrors the Demerged Company's on the Record Date; no promoter stake figures or incentives given
judge.hidden_value: Cost-of-acquisition apportionment splits the pre-demerger cost 53.12% to SKF Industrial versus 46.88% to SKF India, implying the industrial business is the larger piece; 4,94,37,963 shares issued 1:1.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Documents give 1:1 allotment to all shareholders and BSE/NSE listing, but say nothing on size, index membership or holder mix.
judge.listing_timeline: Not dated beyond: 17 October 2025 letter says the Resulting Company "will make necessary application(s) for the purpose of listing", shares "frozen till the time listing / trading permission is granted"; 28 November 2025 compliance letter says listing and commencement of trading must occur "within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT" (NCLT order dated 26 September 2025), which the Resulting Company "shall endeavour to comply" with.

rationale.rationale: Management says SKF India is demerging its Industrial business into a new entity, SKF India (Industrial) Limited, leaving Automotive in the listed SKF India Limited, not to fix a problem but because the two businesses have diverged: 'external' drivers differ (Industrial is driven by infrastructure spend and China Plus One; Automotive by EVs and CAFE norms), customer needs differ (Industrial serves many verticals such as steel, heavy, metals, railways, wind; Automotive serves a few large OEMs plus aftermarket), and manufacturing philosophy differs (one needs large-batch processing, the other shorter cycle times, smaller batches and more innovative products). The stated purpose is 'two fit-for-purpose independent companies' that can each accelerate growth and profitability, with independent management focus (separate board, leadership, sales and manufacturing teams), tailored innovation, tailored capital deployment, higher manufacturing efficiency, more agility, and better standalone visibility for investors. Management repeatedly stressed the split is not driven by weakness: FY25 revenue was about Rs 5,000 crore with 17.2% EBITDA, 11.5% PBT, ROCE 28%-29% and ROE 21%-22%, and a five-year CAGR of 16.4% in revenue, 17.4% in PBT and 17.5% in EPS. On economics, carve-out financials submitted to SEBI showed FY23-24 margins of roughly 14%-15% for both sides, similar despite very different mixes because Automotive is 95% localized while Industrial is only about 40% localized and carries more traded product; management expects Industrial margins to normalize upward as localization rises (overall over 80% of components now sourced locally, with a further ~5 percentage point gain targeted in 3-4 years). The split also reclassifies the tractor business (agriculture and electricals), today reported under Automotive, into Industrial, which is why the scheme shows Industrial at 63% of FY24 revenue versus the ~50%-54% quoted in quarterly commentary. Asset allocation was disclosed progressively: Haridwar 100% Automotive (4 lines), Bangalore 7 of 10 lines and ~85% of land to Automotive, Pune 12 of 22 lines Automotive and 10 Industrial with land split 52:48 and a new Industrial factory to be built next to the existing Automotive plant, and manpower 55%-60% Automotive versus 40%-45% Industrial. Costs of the split are real and visible: Q1 FY26 margins fell 530 basis points, partly from one-time demerger IT and consultant costs that management said will continue for the next year to year and a half.
rationale.evolution: By the Feb 13, 2025 Q3 FY25 call the scheme was already filed with the exchanges and three years of carve-out financials were with SEBI, so the discussion was defensive and definitional - reconciling 63% versus 54% Industrial revenue, auto-versus-industrial margins and localization - with investors (Mukesh Saraf, Viraj Kacharia, Ravi Purohit) pressing for pro forma segment numbers ahead of a shareholder vote. Management then held a dedicated Demerger Update Call on April 09, 2025 devoted to rationale, pro forma financials and timeline, and the May 19, 2025 Q4 call formalized the 'two fit-for-purpose independent companies' language and first disclosed the plant-level split (Haridwar to Automotive, Bangalore 80%-85% Automotive, Pune split with a new Industrial factory). The June 30, 2025 investor meet went deeper: it named the external drivers (infrastructure and China Plus One versus EVs and CAFE norms), gave the first forward split guidance (Automotive 10%-12%, Industrial 8%-10% growth to FY28, Industrial faster thereafter, 17%-19% EBITDA maintained), and confirmed separate boards and leadership before the effective date. By the Aug 07, 2025 Q1 FY26 call the rationale was unchanged but execution detail and cost arrived - line-by-line, land and manpower splits, shareholder approval obtained July 14, 2025, NCLT decision expected September - and the scheme documents then record the NSE observation letter of March 28, 2025, the NCLT filing of April 09, 2025, the October 15, 2025 record date and the October 17, 2025 allotment of 4,94,37,963 shares.

rationale.rationale: The separation management actually explains on these calls is the carve-out and demerger of the Softgel business and Stelis Biopharma (biologics/CDMO) into OneSource Specialty Pharma, announced in the quarter ended Sept 2023 and valued, as the analyst's number was confirmed by Arun Kumar, at around 17x FY24 EBITDA for both softgel and Steriscience. The stated purpose was to combine a very high-margin soft gelatin business with the biologics/drug-device platform to create a 'unique specialty CDMO platform' with a large GLP-1-led contract manufacturing order book (about 15 customers; patents partially off in FY25, main patents only in 2030, so revenue was development/R&D income today and commercial later), and to let Strides shareholders 'participate in value discovery' by holding 44% of OneSource (61% total public shareholding across the three companies). The second, equally explicit driver was balance-sheet repair: against roughly INR3,000 crores of debt, management said the announcement 'solves for the debt to EBITDA ratio' because the combined EBITDA of the two demerged companies was about INR1,200 crores, and INR283 crores of debt moved with the demerger. Third, it ended Strides' contingent exposure to Stelis — corporate guarantees were cut by almost INR600 crores by Feb 2024, with Arun Kumar saying all guarantees 'will go off the book' once listed; by Jan 2025 all guarantees were fully released and by May 2025 the entire INR705 crores of guarantees to Stelis had been closed. Lenders were a direct constituency: all significant NOCs from lenders were obtained, and lenders were accepting because 'there will also be that much less loans in OneSource'; OneSource also gained the ability to raise up to $100 million at relisting, with a bridge facility only until then. Post-demerger the retained Strides business was restated from an April 1, 2024 appointed date and reframed as a focused, bottom-line-led generics business (12%-15% revenue CAGR but much faster EBITDA CAGR), with Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin 18.2%, gross margins held at 58%-59%, ROCE 14.9% vs 9.7% comparable, net debt/EBITDA down to 1.9x, and a INR3,188 crores accounting gain on demerger; management quantified the shareholder outcome as INR78.8 billion distributed 'in the form of demerger and listing'. Note that the filing text supplied here is a different, later transaction — the demerger of Arco Lab's Life Sciences and Digital Innovation business into Pivot Path (appointed date April 10, 2025; NCLT Bengaluru approval May 18/20, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) — and these documents are procedural intimations that contain no rationale section at all.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaces as an already-announced carve-out in the Sept 25, 2023 call ([Oct 2023]), where valuation (~17x FY24 EBITDA), the 44%/61% shareholding slides and the debt-to-EBITDA fix are debated; the Oct 30, 2023 call ([Nov 2023]) fleshes out the industrial logic (GLP-1 drug-device order book, ~15 customers, patents opening 2025-2030). By the Feb 2024 call it is an execution story — exchange queries, NOCs from lenders, guarantees down INR600 crores, NCLT filing targeted that quarter — and in May 2024 SEBI approval arrives as 'the last step' before a 3-4 quarter court process plus ~60 days to list. The Jan 30, 2025 call ([Feb 2025]) reports it done: OneSource listed, appointed date April 1, 2024, financials restated, all guarantees released; May 2025 and July 2025 ([Aug 2025]) use it as the proof point (INR705 crores guarantees closed, INR78.8 billion distributed, OneSource stake retained as 'a great strategic outcome'), and by May 2026 the softgel exit is only a footnote to resetting the US aspiration to $375-$400 million for FY28.

rationale.rationale: The supplied material contains no earnings-call passages at all — only a truncated NCLT order (CP(CAA)/55(AHM)2025 in CA(CAA)/41(AHM)2025, lead petitioner JKPL Utility Packaging Solutions Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.) — so the reasoning below is the filing's alone, and it is stated entirely in placeholder terms (Transferor Companies 1-4, Transferee Company) with no business names, no financial figures and no identified requesting party. The scheme is a multi-part restructuring rather than a described spin-off: (a) three wholly-owned subsidiaries (Transferors 1-3) amalgamate into the Transferee Company because they are in a 'similar line of business' and the boards decided to consolidate all packaging manufacturing and trading entities under one roof, which is expected to give more efficient use of capital assets, supply chain and customer relationships, flexibility in funding the Transferors' capex, elimination of intra-group transactions and the 'cash flow blockages' they cause, fewer shareholding tiers, fewer duplicated legal and regulatory compliances, and savings on administration of separate entities. (b) Redeemable Preference Shares held by the Transferee in Transferor Company 4 are reduced and converted into an unsecured loan so the investment is reflected 'as a liability' — the filing says this is what 'facilitate[s] the demerger from the Transferor Company 4' under Part D — and that loan is then cancelled automatically when Transferor 4 merges in under Part F; the filing asserts this will not impair Transferor 4's liquidity or ability to meet obligations. (c) After Part E, Transferor Company 4 'would be left with paper and packaging business', and because it and the Transferee are in the same line of business, it too is merged in to consolidate all paper and packaging manufacturing and trading entities, again citing structure rationalisation, fewer compliances and lower administrative cost. (d) Reserves are re-organised by setting off the debit balance of Credit Reserve against the existing credit balance 'in order to right-size the balance sheet' so the books 'present a fair representation of the financial position'. Crucially, the demerged business itself — what leaves Transferor Company 4 under Part E, and why — is not described in the excerpt, so the actual separation rationale is absent from the text provided.
rationale.evolution: No earnings calls were provided, so there is no call-by-call evolution to report and none may be supplied from memory. The only datable sequence in the filing is procedural: Appointed Date 01.04.2024; board approval of the scheme on 13.12.2024; documents filed with BSE and NSE on 30.12.2024; stock-exchange observation letters received 08.08.2025; first-motion application filed 15.08.2025 with order 08.09.2025; creditor/shareholder meetings held 01.11.2025 and 02.11.2025 with chairman's report 10.11.2025; second-motion petition filed 12.11.2025 (e-filed 07.11.2025); notice order 20.11.2025, affidavit of service 11.12.2025; RD representation 12.12.2025 and RoC report 18.11.2025, answered by joint affidavit 17.12.2025. The Regional Director objected that the Appointed Date was ante-dated more than a year before filing contrary to MCA Circular 09/2019, and that assets, liabilities and reserves should transfer at standalone rather than consolidated carrying values.

points.point: Transferors 1-3 are wholly-owned subsidiaries in a similar line of business; the boards decided to consolidate all packaging manufacturing and trading entities under the Transferee Company to use capital assets, supply chain and customer relationships more efficiently.
points.quote: The Transferor Company 1, Transferor Company 2, Transferor Company 3, and the Transferee Company are engaged in similar line of business, and the Board of the respective companies has decided to consolidate all packaging business, manufacturing, and trading entities under the Transferee Company.

points.point: A stated purpose is capex funding flexibility for the three subsidiaries and the removal of intra-group transactions that were trapping cash within the group.
points.quote: Facilitate flexibility in funding the capex of the Transferor Company 1, Transferor Company 2, Transferor Company 3, eliminate intra-group transactions and consequent cash flow blockages which shall result in efficient utilization of capital

points.point: The reduction and conversion of Redeemable Preference Shares into an unsecured loan is explicitly the enabling step for the demerger out of Transferor Company 4, by restating the investment as a liability.
points.quote: The reduction and conversion of Redeemable Preference Shares (RPS) in the manner proposed in the Scheme would enable the Transferee Company to reflect the true nature of investment in the Transferor Company 4 i.e., as a liability, and thereby, facilitate the demerger from the Transferor Company 4 (as a part of the Scheme);

points.point: The converted unsecured loan is cancelled automatically once Transferor Company 4 merges into the Transferee under Part F, with no further instrument required.
points.quote: The RPS issued by Transferor Company 4 (or the Demerged Company) shall, upon the effectiveness of Part D of the Scheme, be converted into an unsecured loan.

points.point: The filing asserts the Part D step leaves Transferor Company 4's liquidity and ability to meet its obligations unaffected.
points.quote: The Scheme would not affect the ability or liquidity of the Transferor Company 4 to meet its obligations/ commitments in the normal course of business upon effectiveness of the Part D of the Scheme.

points.point: After the Part E demerger, Transferor Company 4 retains only the paper and packaging business, which is why it is then merged into the same-line-of-business Transferee Company.
points.quote: Upon effectiveness of Part E of the Scheme, Transferor Company 4 would be left with paper and packaging business and management of Transferor Company 4 and Transferee Company are engaged in the same line of business, and so, the Board of the respective companies have decided to consolidate all paper and packaging business, manufacturing, and trading entities under the Transferee Company;

points.point: Structural simplification is cited for both the amalgamation legs: fewer shareholding tiers and a rationalised corporate structure.
points.quote: Assist in rationalizing the corporate structure and reduction of shareholding tiers.

points.point: Cost and compliance duplication across the separate entities is cited as a problem the consolidation solves.
points.quote: Result in savings of administration and other costs associated with managing separate entities

points.point: The reserve re-organisation sets off the debit balance of Credit Reserve against existing credit balances explicitly to right-size the balance sheet and present a fair view.
points.quote: The Scheme proposes to set off the debit balance of Credit Reserve arising out of effectiveness of the Scheme as on the Appointed Date against the existing credit balance lying under Transferee Company, in order to right-size the balance sheet;

points.point: The regulator challenged the 01.04.2024 Appointed Date as ante-dated more than a year before the 15.08.2025 filing, with no justification in the scheme as MCA Circular 09/2019 requires.
points.quote: In the scheme, no justification has mentioned about gap of more than one year in filing of application and appointed date.

points.point: The petitioners attributed the delay to the listed Transferee's stock-exchange observation process, which took from 30.12.2024 to 08.08.2025.
points.quote: The Transferee Company received the observation letters from the stock exchanges on 08.08.2025.

points.point: The RoC/RD also objected that transfers should be at standalone, not consolidated, carrying values as paras 11.1 and 11.2 provide.
points.quote: In this regard, it is submitted that all the Assets, Liabilities and reserves of the Transferor Companies are required to be transferred at the respective carrying values in the standalone financial statements of the Transferee Company instead of consolidated financial statements.

rationale.what_management_expects: Only group-level effects are stated: consolidation of all packaging, then paper-and-packaging, manufacturing and trading entities under the Transferee Company; more efficient use of capital assets, supply chain and customer relationships; capex funding flexibility; no intra-group cash-flow blockages; fewer shareholding tiers, compliances and administrative costs; and a right-sized balance sheet. Nothing on margins, valuation or per-entity outcomes.

rationale.rationale: No earnings-call passages were supplied with this request — the "CALL PASSAGES" section is empty — so everything below comes solely from the Regulation 30 filings dated 1st October, 2026 and the scheme rationale section. The transaction is not a spin-off of a business out of the listed company but the reverse: a demerger of the "Sunteck City 4th Avenue Undertaking", a residential real estate project, out of Satguru Corporate Services Private Limited (the Demerged Company, a wholly owned subsidiary) and into Sunteck Realty Limited (the Resulting Company, the listed entity), on a going concern basis under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013. Management characterises it twice in the filing as "essentially an internal reorganisation between Sunteck and its wholly owned subsidiary - Satguru." The stated benefits are three: consolidation of the Demerged Business Undertaking; achieving administrative and operational efficiencies; and efficient pooling and deployment of financial and managerial resources so as to "facilitate project-specific capital allocation and funding strategies." The only quantification given is scale: the Demerged Business Undertaking's turnover for the year ended 31 March 2026 was Rs. ~869 Crs, representing ~77% of Sunteck's total consolidated turnover for FY ended 31st March 2026 — i.e. the group's dominant revenue stream currently sits one level below the listed entity, which is the structural anomaly the scheme removes. Because Satguru is wholly owned, no shares are issued, there is no cash consideration and no share exchange ratio, there is no change in the shareholding patterns of either company, and no fresh listing is required since Sunteck's equity shares are already listed on the Stock Exchanges. The scheme remains subject to requisite statutory and regulatory approvals including the approval of the National Company Law Tribunal. The same board meeting (6.45 p.m. to 7.05 p.m. on Thursday, 1st October, 2026) also approved, on the Audit Committee's recommendation, the appointment of Ernst & Young LLP as Internal Auditor up to 31st March, 2027.
rationale.evolution: No call-by-call evolution can be reconstructed: no earnings-call passages were provided, so there is no dated record of how or when the idea surfaced or changed. The only dated evidence is 1st October, 2026, when the Board of Directors approved the Scheme of Arrangement and the company disclosed it to NSE (Symbol: SUNTECK) and BSE (Scrip Code: 512179) under Regulation 30 read with the SEBI Master Circular dated 30th January, 2026. The filing presents the rationale as settled and final, with no reference to prior discussion, to investor, lender or partner requests, or to any earlier version of the plan.

rationale.rationale: L&T is not spinning off to shareholders — it is transferring its Realty Undertaking as a going concern to L&T Realty Properties Limited (LTRPL), a wholly-owned subsidiary, by slump sale under a Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013, at an enterprise value of ₹6,300 Cr, with consideration discharged in fully paid-up equity shares of LTRPL issued to L&T, so there is no dilution of shareholding and no change in ownership, voting rights or shareholder interests. Management's stated trigger is that the Realty business has grown in scale and complexity: it has an estimated development potential of approximately 71 million sq ft across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Bengaluru, NCR and Chennai, achieved pre-sales of approximately ₹10,000 Cr in FY2025-26 (the May 2026 call described this as pre-sales more than doubling to ₹94 billion, aided by launches in Noida and Panvel), yet contributed only about 0.59% of consolidated revenue — a business too big to run as a business unit but too small to be visible inside the parent. The Board's fix is a dedicated platform giving sharper strategic focus, greater operating agility and enhanced managerial accountability, while the business keeps the L&T brand, governance standards and institutional strengths. The structure is also explicitly a capital-raising and partnering vehicle: it is said to provide greater flexibility to access growth capital, attract strategic partners and engage with sector-focused investors, supporting a five-year plan of accelerated pre-sales growth through land acquisitions, joint developments and selective expansion of the commercial portfolio. A second problem solved is group structure: the Jan 2026 and May 2026 calls frame this as the start of a phased consolidation of all group real estate undertakings into one simplified, scalable platform, rather than assets scattered across entities. Management states the reorganisation has no material impact on L&T's engineering, manufacturing, technology and infrastructure businesses, and that employees, customer relationships, ongoing projects, contracts, approvals and licences move across without interruption. It is presented as part of a wider portfolio clean-up — alongside the concession exits, where SPAs were executed to divest 100% of Nabha Power and L&T's entire stake in Hyderabad Metro, both expected to close in Q1 FY27 — aimed at enhancing capital allocation flexibility and improving valuation visibility.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaces publicly on the Jan 2026 call, where management says the parent has 'initiated' the transfer of the Realty undertaking to LTRPL via slump sale under a Scheme of Arrangement subject to regulatory approvals, and frames it as the start of a phased consolidation of all real estate assets into a unified platform for scale, agility and financial strength. By the May 2026 call the framing has shifted from announcement to execution and justification: the scheme is described as an approved NCLT scheme of arrangement, consolidation of all group real estate undertakings into a single simplified, scalable structure is called the year's primary focus for Realty, and the business's operating momentum is cited as evidence — pre-sales more than doubling to ₹94 billion in FY26 on Noida and Panvel launches — while concession exits (Nabha Power, Hyderabad Metro) run in parallel. The scheme filing then adds the hard terms and the fuller rationale absent from the calls: the ₹6,300 Cr enterprise value, share-based consideration, ~71 million sq ft development potential, the 0.59% revenue contribution, no shareholder dilution, and the capital-access/valuation-visibility arguments. Shareholders approved it at the NCLT-convened meeting of August 4, 2026 (116 members attending) with the requisite majority, following NCLT orders dated June 12, 16 and 25, 2026.

points.point: The Chairman pre-empts the main investor fear: this is an internal transfer to a wholly-owned subsidiary with no dilution and no change in shareholder rights.
points.quote: At the outset, let me reassure you that this proposal does not involve any dilution of your shareholding in L&T.

points.point: Scale and complexity are given as the trigger; the remedy is a dedicated platform with focus, agility and accountability, while retaining L&T brand and governance.
points.quote: As the business has grown in scale and complexity, the Board believes that the time is right to house the Realty business under a dedicated platform that can provide sharper strategic focus, greater operating agility and enhanced managerial accountability, while continuing to benefit from the L&T brand, governance standards and institutional strengths built over decades.

points.point: The size mismatch is quantified: ~71 million sq ft of development potential across five metros, ₹10,000 Cr FY26 pre-sales, but only ~0.59% of consolidated revenue.
points.quote: During FY 2025-26, L&T Realty Business Unit achieved pre-sales of approximately ₹ 10,000 Crs and contributed about 0.59 % of the consolidated revenue.

points.point: Capital and partnership access is an explicit objective — the structure is meant to court growth capital, strategic partners and sector-focused (real-estate specialist) investors.
points.quote: The proposed structure will also provide greater flexibility to access growth capital, attract strategic partners and engage with sector-focused investors.

points.point: Consideration terms: slump sale on a going-concern basis at ₹6,300 Cr enterprise value, paid for in LTRPL equity shares issued to L&T (no cash leaves the group).

points.point: Stated outcomes for shareholders: capital allocation flexibility and better valuation visibility for the realty assets, which are currently buried in the consolidated entity.
points.quote: It will create a stronger platform for growth, enhance capital allocation flexibility, improve valuation visibility and position the Realty business to capitalize on the significant opportunities emerging in India's real estate sector.

points.point: Ring-fencing assurance: the core engineering/manufacturing/infrastructure franchise is unaffected, and employees, customers, projects and contracts transfer seamlessly.
points.quote: The proposed reorganisation does not have any material impact on the Company's broader engineering, manufacturing, technology and infrastructure businesses, while enabling the Realty business to pursue its growth ambitions through a more focused and agile framework.

points.point: Growth plan the platform is meant to fund: accelerated pre-sales growth over five years via land acquisitions, joint developments and selective commercial expansion.
points.quote: Building on this momentum, the business is targeting pre-sales growth at an accelerated rate over the next five years, supported by a disciplined growth strategy focused on land acquisitions, joint developments, and selective expansion of the commercial portfolio.

points.point: Process milestone: shareholders approved the scheme by requisite majority at the NCLT-convened meeting on August 4, 2026, held after NCLT orders of June 12/16/25, 2026, with 116 members attending.
points.quote: Basis the above, we declare that the resolution as set out in the NCLT Convened Meeting Notice has been duly passed by the shareholders through e-voting process with requisite majority.

rationale.rationale: The separation in question is the carve-out of Cyient's Semiconductor business (turnkey ASIC) out of the parent into a dedicated entity, Cyient Semiconductor — not a demerger of Cyient DLM, which management explicitly declined to separate further. Management's stated logic (July 25, 2024 call, tagged Aug 2024) was that Cyient already had a rare end-to-end semiconductor capability — it can "design these chips, ... fabricate these chips, test these chips, prototype these chips and sell these chips" by leveraging design, FAB, OSAT and testing — and that in a market shifting to analog/sensory-to-digital chips, this deserved a business that could "exclusively and dedicatedly focus on turnkey ASIC" rather than sit inside a services P&L. The explicit template was Cyient DLM: the opportunity was framed "along the lines with the value unlock of Cyient DLM," i.e. a separate structure with its own capital and its own independently established value. The Board approved the spin-off into a different entity (May 2025 call), a dedicated CEO was hired (Suman Narayan for Cyient Semiconductor; Sukamal Banerjee became CEO for the DET business), and by the Jul 2025 call the carve-out was "completed as planned," with the group moving to four reported segments — DET, Semiconductor (a separate subsidiary "with its own leaders, with its own management and with its own structure"), DLM and Others — and DET numbers restated to exclude Semiconductor so the core services business could be judged like-for-like. The problem being solved is structural mismatch: Semiconductor is to be "run as a start-up investment positioned for accelerated growth," which needs capital and risk tolerance that would otherwise dilute the parent's margin and growth optics. The demand side was cited as external pull — "significant interest in the business from our customers, our partners and investors" — with order intake in the first post-carve-out quarter exceeding budget by about 10%. By Apr 2026 the financing was explicitly bifurcated: a buyback at the Cyient level (the Board judging it the right time given capital requirements and where the share price "is and has been") versus a separate fundraise at Cyient Semiconductor to "establish an independent value," sized not large but enough to carry it to breakeven, expected towards the end of a period the transcript cuts off. In Jul 2026, asked by ChrysCapital for a clean DLM demerger, Krishna Bodanapu refused on operating grounds — DLM and Cyient are mutually dependent, engineering deals are won because of the manufacturing capability — confirming that separation is applied only where there is no such interdependence.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Aug 2024 (July 25, 2024) call as an intention to create a separate turnkey-ASIC business, pitched explicitly as a repeat of the Cyient DLM value unlock. The Feb 2025 call did not advance the separation — it was about internal sales/performance re-engineering (a new large-deal function, a performance framework rewarding revenue and margin growth, 13 large deals in Q3). By May 2025 Board approval for the spin-off was in hand and Suman Narayan was named CEO of Cyient Semiconductor alongside Sukamal Banerjee taking over DET; the Jul 2025 call declared the carve-out complete, introduced four-segment reporting with DET restated ex-Semiconductor, and reported order intake ~10% above budget. Apr 2026 moved it to the capital stage — a Cyient-level buyback alongside a separate Cyient Semiconductor fundraise to establish independent value and fund the path to breakeven — while Jul 2026 drew the boundary by ruling out a DLM demerger for now.

rationale.rationale: On these texts alone, there is no stated rationale for separating a business — the documents describe the opposite transaction plus one unrelated operational 'carve-out'. The Jan 2026 filing is a cover letter for a joint call on 'announcement of merger through a Scheme of Arrangement involving Sapphire Foods India Limited ("Transferor Company"), Devyani International Limited ("Transferee Company")' — an amalgamation of Sapphire into Devyani, not a demerger, and the transcript body itself is truncated before any management reasoning is given. The only 'carve out' language anywhere is operational, from the May 2025 call, where CFO Manish Dawar explained how KFC can still earn roughly 20% restaurant operating margin at about Rs.105k ADS: new KFC openings had cannibalised existing stores, so Devyani is resizing formats, carving physical space inside KFC stores for 'newer brands, which are very small kiosk type of formats', and saying 'These brands will be independent' — independence of brand/format within a store, with no mention of a legal entity, scheme, or shareholder event. Supporting margin levers he cited were format change, labour and overhead synergies if ADS stays soft, and continuous landlord rent negotiation. The so-called scheme rationale text supplied is not a rationale at all: it is the NSE observation letter and BSE letter of June 12, 2026 conveying SEBI's comments and 'No objection' under Regulation 37, which merely *require* the companies to disclose 'The rationale and objectives underlying the proposed scheme' to shareholders — the rationale is demanded, never stated. The only shareholder-structure specifics given are a separate SFIL Secondary Sale of up to 5,94,55,837 equity shares, up to 18.5% of Sapphire's share capital as of December 31, 2025, from Sapphire Foods Mauritius Limited to Arctic International Limited, promoter/promoter-group entities of Sapphire and Devyani 'intending to be reclassified in the Public Category in Devyani', and a condition that the scheme be expressly subject to Competition Commission of India approval before NCLT filing.
rationale.evolution: May 2025: carve-out appears only as a store-level idea — space inside cannibalised KFC stores for small kiosk-format 'independent' brands, as one lever to defend ~20% ROM at ~Rs.105k ADS. January 6, 2026 (transcript filed January 13, 2026): the corporate action announced is a merger, Sapphire Foods as transferor into Devyani as transferee, with the SFIL Secondary Sale of up to 18.5% of Sapphire measured as of December 31, 2025 sitting alongside it. June 12, 2026: NSE and BSE issue Regulation 37 observation/no-objection letters adding CCI approval as a pre-NCLT condition and ordering disclosure of the rationale, cost-benefit analysis, valuation methods and promoter reclassification. Across the three documents the direction of travel is consolidation plus promoter reclassification, not separation.

rationale.rationale: The supplied texts do not actually contain a stated rationale for a separation — they document two separation-adjacent moves without management's reasoning. The only concrete separation described is the hive-off of NTPC's coal mining business into its wholly-owned subsidiary NTPC Mining Limited (NML): a business transfer agreement was signed at an estimated value of ₹10,503 crore, the Chatti Bariatu and Badam mines had already been transferred as of the October 30, 2025 call, and management said it expects to complete transfer of all remaining mines to NML within the current fiscal. The second thread is NTPC Green Energy, raised only as an investor question in the July 2024 call, where Atul Mehra of Motilal Oswal Asset Management asked whether NTPC would do a 'full-fledged demerger' of NTPC Green or keep it substantially held by NTPC with only a minority offloaded in the IPO — the passage ends before any management answer is given. Critically, the document labelled 'scheme rationale' is not a demerger scheme at all: it is a Regulation 30 intimation dated 28th November 2025 that the NCLT, Delhi approved the resolution plan of the NTPC–MAHAGENCO consortium for Sinnar Thermal Power Limited, a 5x270 MW (1,350 MW) coal-based plant at Sinnar, Nashik, Maharashtra, under CIRP per the IBC — an acquisition, not a separation. So on these texts the structure is: coal mining carved into NML by business transfer at ₹10,503 crore, renewables housed in NTPC Green with an IPO, and no articulated problem being solved, no lender or partner demand, and no margin, capital-allocation or valuation argument on record. The 28th November 2025 filing adds nothing to the separation story, as it concerns the Sinnar Thermal acquisition via CIRP. There is no call in between that explains the shift from investor question to executed carve-out.

rationale.rationale: These texts do not contain a demerger or spin-off rationale for Coal India — there is no scheme of arrangement and no rationale section in the filings supplied. What the filings actually document is partial monetisation of wholly-owned coal subsidiaries through minority IPOs structured as Offers for Sale by CIL, not a separation of a business line. The trigger stated is governmental, not strategic: the Ministry of Coal, via Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 dated 16.12.2025, 'advised CIL to take concrete steps to ensure further listing of subsidiaries namely MCL and SECL in the upcoming financial year,' after which the CIL Board gave in-principle approval by circular resolution on 23.12.2025 for both Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) and South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL), to be routed to MoC for onward submission to DIPAM. The executed transaction is Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL): 465,700,000 equity shares of face value ₹10 offered for sale by CIL at ₹23 per share, listed on BSE and NSE effective 19.01.2026, cutting CIL's holding from 100% to 90% (4,657,000,000 to 4,191,300,000 shares), so BCCL ceased to be a wholly-owned subsidiary but remains a subsidiary. The next step is MCL's DRHP dated 1 September 2026, filed with SEBI, BSE and NSE, for an OFS of up to 661,836,300 equity shares of face value ₹2 held by CIL, subject to approvals and market conditions. The only earnings-call passage provided (Feb 2024) runs the other way: asked directly whether renewables/CIL energy would be put into a demerged entity, management said existing subsidiaries and JVs already cover those verticals and that no new entity was under discussion. The sole capital-structure specifics management gave in that call were that coal mine capex would be met from internal accruals, with little debt in FY25 but rising debt in the following year for the renewal and gasification projects. On this evidence the separation is a state-directed stake sale/listing programme for coal-producing subsidiaries (BCCL done, MCL filed, SECL approved in principle), with no management-stated operating or valuation argument on record here.
rationale.evolution: Feb 2024 call: an analyst (Venkatesh Subramanian) raised a demerger of the energy/renewables verticals and management rejected it — subsidiaries and JVs already exist, 'It is not in our discussion right now.' The impetus then came from outside the company: MoC's OM of 16.12.2025 directed further listing of MCL and SECL, and CIL's Board passed in-principle approvals for both on 23.12.2025 for onward submission to DIPAM. Execution followed quickly on a different subsidiary — BCCL disclosures on 03.01.2026 and 14.01.2026, pricing at ₹23 and listing on 19.01.2026 taking CIL to 90%. The programme then advanced to MCL with a DRHP dated 01.09.2026, disclosed 02.09.2026, for an OFS of up to 661,836,300 shares; SECL remains at in-principle stage in these texts.

points.point: An analyst explicitly asked whether coal, CIL energy and the alternative-energy investments would be split into a separate demerged entity; management declined, saying the verticals already sit in existing subsidiaries and JVs and no new entity was being considered.

We had already formed the joint ventures and the new companies, so those we'll pursue that. We are not going to create any new subsidy. It is not in our discussion right now.

rationale.rationale: The texts describe a consolidation rather than a separation: Craftsman Automation Ltd. (BSE 543276 / NSE CRAFTSMAN) is pulling its aluminium products business together inside one wholly owned subsidiary, not carving a business out. Per the scheme rationale, the Amalgamating Company 3 ("DRA") manufactures precision-engineered aluminium die-cast components, sub-assemblies and products primarily for the automotive sector in India, while the Amalgamated Company ("Sunbeam") is also engaged in manufacturing of aluminium components and related activities — so two entities hold the same business. Separately, Amalgamating Company 2 is in development, ownership and leasing of industrial, logistics and warehousing projects and related infrastructure, and owns land parcels leased to DRA; Amalgamating Company 1 is a wholly owned subsidiary of DRA, and these recently acquired step-down subsidiaries hold land parcels leased to DRA for the development and expansion of its aluminium manufacturing facilities. Management's stated problem is fragmentation: "the Aluminium business and the land and infrastructure required for its expansion are housed in different entities, resulting in the fragmentation of operations and asset ownership." Their stated opportunity is that the aluminium components industry "is poised for substantial growth," which can be "better capitalized" by one focused operating entity with a stronger balance sheet, a broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership and a streamlined organisational structure. The immediate operational trigger is that DRA's board has approved setting up a new aluminium facility on the land parcels leased from the step-down subsidiaries, so consolidation is expected to deliver efficient implementation of the approved expansion plans, seamless development of manufacturing facilities, and alignment of land, infrastructure and operations under a single entity. Mechanically, Companies 1 and 2 merge into DRA with no shares issued (wholly owned), then DRA merges into Sunbeam, whose equity is re-denominated to INR 1 face value and which issues 1 share of INR 1 at a premium of INR 9 for each INR 10 face-value DRA share; the listed company is not a party and its shareholding pattern is unaffected.
rationale.evolution: No earnings call passages were supplied with this prompt, so the idea cannot be traced call by call and no call dates are available. The only dated step in these texts is the board meeting of Friday, 13th February 2026 (5:00–5:15 P.M.), at which the board approved only the initiation of an evaluation process for a potential internal restructuring/consolidation of the aluminium products business at a single wholly owned subsidiary level, plus consolidation of other wholly owned subsidiaries, expressly leaving the mode open (including a scheme of arrangement under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013) and the final decision to a later board. The scheme rationale filing is the later stage, where that open-ended evaluation has crystallised into a specific three-step amalgamation of Companies 1 and 2 into DRA and of DRA into Sunbeam, with a stated share exchange ratio.

points.point: The core stated problem is structural fragmentation: the aluminium manufacturing business sits in one set of entities while the land and infrastructure needed for its expansion sit in others, splitting operations from asset ownership.
points.quote: At present, the Aluminium business and the land and infrastructure required for its expansion are housed in different entities, resulting in the fragmentation of operations and asset ownership.

points.point: Duplication is explicit — DRA and Sunbeam are both in the same aluminium components business, which is why they are being merged into one.
points.quote: DRA and Sunbeam are both engaged in manufacturing of Aluminium Components and related activities.

points.point: The growth case: management says the aluminium components industry is set for substantial growth, framing the restructuring as positioning for that growth rather than as a fix for weakness.
points.quote: The Management of the Companies are of the view that the Aluminium Components Industry is poised for substantial growth.

points.point: The four claimed benefits of a single focused operating entity are named precisely: stronger balance sheet, broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership, streamlined organisation.
points.quote: This opportunity can be better capitalized by consolidating the Aluminium business under a single focused operating entity having a stronger balance sheet, a broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership, and a streamlined organizational structure.

points.point: The concrete trigger is an already-approved greenfield project: DRA's board has sanctioned a new aluminium plant on land it currently only leases from the recently acquired step-down subsidiaries.
points.quote: The Board of DRA has approved the setting up of a new Aluminium facility on the land parcels leased from the Step Down Subsidiaries.

points.point: Merging the landholding step-down subsidiaries into DRA is justified on execution grounds — faster build-out and ownership of land, infrastructure and operations in one entity instead of an intra-group lease.
points.quote: It is expected that consolidation of the Step-Down Subsidiaries with DRA will lead to efficient implementation of the approved expansion plans, seamless development of manufacturing facilities, and align ownership of land, infrastructure, and operations under a single entity.

points.point: The final leg (DRA into Sunbeam) is justified on holding-structure grounds rather than operational ones.
points.quote: The proposed consolidation of DRA with Sunbeam is also expected to simplify the corporate structure and improve managerial focus and operational efficiency.

points.point: The lessor entity's business is broader than auto components — it is an industrial/logistics/warehousing property vehicle whose land is leased to the aluminium manufacturer.
points.quote: Amalgamating Company 2 owns land parcels which it has leased to Amalgamating Company 3 for its use.

points.point: The business being consolidated is precision aluminium die-casting for Indian automotive customers.
points.quote: The Amalgamating Company 3 is engaged in the manufacturing of precision-engineered Aluminium die-cast components, sub-assemblies, and products primarily for the automotive sector in India.

points.point: Consideration: the two wholly owned legs are share-less, and DRA's shareholders get a 1:1 swap into Sunbeam after Sunbeam's face value is reset from INR 10 to INR 1, with INR 9 of each new share booked as premium.
points.quote: After reorganization of the equity capital of the Amalgamated Company such that the face value of its equity shares is changed to INR 1/- each, issuance of 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of the Amalgamated Company having face value of INR 1/- (Indian Rupees One) each at a premium of INR 9/- (Indian Rupees Nine) each, for every 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of face value INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each held in the Amalgamating Company 3.

rationale.what_management_expects: Merged aluminium entity: stronger balance sheet, broader product and manufacturing base, unified land/asset ownership, streamlined structure, efficient execution of the board-approved new facility, better capture of expected industry growth. Group: simpler structure, improved managerial focus and operational efficiency. No margin, capital or valuation figures given; the listed company's shareholding pattern is unaffected.

rationale.rationale: On these texts alone, there is no demerger or spin-off of a pharmaceutical business being explained — the only 'separation' documented is a non-core asset exit: at its July 11, 2026 board meeting Mankind approved divesting 100% of Broadway Hospitality Services Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, to AKRK Projects LLP and Partners for ₹49.00 crore (subject to closing adjustment), to be completed within 90 days, with the stated reason being 'the Company's strategy to divest it's non-core assets'. The size disclosures make the logic plain: Broadway contributed FY26 revenue of ₹9.63 crore (0.07% of the company), total income ₹9.90 crore (0.07%) and net worth ₹38.99 crore (0.24%) — a hospitality business immaterial to a pharma company, sold to a non-promoter, non-related party. The same board approved the opposite leg of the reshaping: a new Netherlands wholly owned subsidiary as an SPV to hold R&D assets and do business development in niche therapies, through joint ventures or strategic interests, with investment of up to EUR 5 million in tranches — i.e. cash out of non-core hospitality, capital into focused R&D/in-licensing. A third, earlier step in the same clean-up was the April 13, 2026 approval to wind up Mankind Pharma Lanka (Private) Limited, a non-operating, non-material Sri Lankan WOS, because 'changed regulatory requirements' made the anticipated business objectives no longer viable. The earnings calls supply the cultural/structural argument rather than any scheme rationale: on Jan 2025 management cited the OTC business as precedent, where they corrected practices by 'hiving off', cutting the number of distributors and bringing in outside talent so one leader no longer ran OTC and pharma together, after which growth improved, and said 80–90% of the analogous changes in the Mankind Pharma Delhi division were complete with one quarter to go. The Nov 2024 call frames the productivity problem behind that focus push: the chronic-focused specialty division has productivity below the company average, newer specialty divisions (MD/DM/KOL-facing, launched in the last 3–4 years) run at about ₹3 lakh PCPM against ₹8–10 lakh in the legacy multi-specialty divisions carrying brands like Telmikind and Amlokind (₹400–500 crore each), and acute versus chronic cannot be carved out because divisions were launched as multi-specialty; chronic was ~28% of the mix five years ago. On BSV, management argued the acquired business is 'a totally different ball game' — super-specialty, critical care, gynec, IVF — with only 5–10% overlap, the exception being the TTK portfolio's 3–4 branded-prescription divisions that move to the Delhi side for optimisation; BSV's PCPM averaged 6.5 last year, but excluding TTK (under 3) the rest is upwards of ₹8 lakh.
rationale.evolution: Nov 05, 2024: the groundwork is diagnostic rather than structural — low-productivity chronic/specialty divisions (~₹3 lakh PCPM vs ₹8–10 lakh legacy), an admission that acute and chronic cannot be carved out of multi-specialty divisions, and BSV described as near-zero overlap except the TTK divisions to be re-homed to Delhi. Jan 2025: the method is named, with OTC as the template — 'hiving off', separate leadership for OTC versus pharma, distributor rationalisation and outside hires — and management says 80–90% of the same changes in the Delhi division are done, one quarter remaining. Then a gap in the supplied record until April 13, 2026, when the board winds up the dormant Sri Lanka WOS, and July 11, 2026, when it converts the 'focus' theme into balance-sheet action: sell Broadway for ₹49 crore as non-core, and seed a Netherlands R&D/niche-therapy SPV with up to EUR 5 million. No call passage here ever discusses the Broadway sale, the Netherlands SPV, or any demerger of a listed business.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Reliance's FMCG arm, Reliance Consumer Products Ltd (RCPL) — the Campa-led consumer brands business — which was carved out of Reliance Retail (held as a 100% subsidiary of RRVL) into a direct subsidiary of Reliance Industries, with RRVL's shareholding simply replicated so Reliance Retail shareholders hold the same stake in the demerged entity. On the Jul 2025 call management framed the logic as the FMCG business having outgrown its host: it had built 'an own independent distribution network, which is pretty substantial', run a high-decibel IPL campaign for Campa with high recall, reached double-digit market share in key markets, and was rapidly expanding supply chain and world-class manufacturing and R&D with heavy automation and backward integration to deliver product superiority and the lowest cost. Management stressed that retail and FMCG already operated at arm's length even inside one group, and the demerger makes 'these two become completely independent' — i.e. it formalises a separation that was already economically real rather than creating new synergies. Timing was gated entirely on regulatory approvals: as of Jul 2025 it was 'not yet' done and 'under regulatory approvals'; the demerger became effective 1 December 2025. The scale cited at demerger was over Rs 5,000 crore of turnover, up 60% year on year, supported by a run of brand purchases. The visible consequence for the parent is reporting optics: RCPL revenue sat inside retail through Q2, so reported retail growth fell to 8.1% (Q3, revenue Rs 97,600 crore, EBITDA Rs 6,915 crore, 8% margin) and 7.4% in the Jun-2026 quarter versus 11.6% underlying, with Q4 growth of 11% becoming almost 14% adjusted and full-year 12%. Notably, management never gave a capital, tax, debt, valuation or listing rationale on any of these calls, and the 'scheme rationale' text supplied here is not the RCPL scheme at all.
rationale.evolution: On the Jul 2025 call the FMCG/Campa update ended with the disclosure that the business 'is in the process of being demerged' out of Reliance Retail into an RIL subsidiary, pending regulatory approvals, with Vikash Jain (CLSA) pressing in Q&A on whether it was done and on shareholder mechanics — answered as a 100% RRVL sub that 'will just move out and shareholding will get replicated'. By the Jan 2026 call it was a completed fact: effective 1 December 2025, Rs 5,000+ crore turnover, up 60%, and the discussion shifted entirely from rationale to accounting impact, with Harit Kapoor (Investec) asking for ex-demerger like-to-like growth and the margin hit from the first full clean quarter. In Apr 2026 and Jul 2026 the demerger appeared only as a reporting adjustment — 11% reported versus almost 14% adjusted in Q4, and 7.4% reported versus 11.6% underlying in Q1 FY27. The 'why' was therefore stated once, early, and never revisited or expanded.

points.point: Management disclosed the FMCG business was being demerged out of Reliance Retail into a direct subsidiary of Reliance Industries, to become an independent business once regulatory approvals were in place.
points.quote: It is in the process of being demerged out of Reliance Retail into a subsidiary of Reliance Industries.

points.point: The core stated rationale: retail and FMCG already dealt with each other at arm's length, and the demerger makes them fully independent rather than changing how they trade.
points.quote: And we have, even today we have an arm's length relationship between our retail business and our FMCG business, but then these two become completely independent.

points.point: Justification by standalone capability — the FMCG business had built its own substantial distribution network, independent of the retail store network.
points.quote: the business has built an own independent distribution network, which is pretty substantial.

points.point: Evidence of standalone brand traction cited just before announcing the demerger: the IPL Campa campaign and double-digit share in key markets.
points.quote: We did a very high decibel campaign during IPL for Campa, which has a very high recall. And we now have double digit market share in key markets.

points.point: The business case for the separate entity rests on its own manufacturing/R&D build-out — automation and backward integration for product superiority and lowest cost.
points.quote: We are using world-class, building world-class manufacturing and R&D facilities with a lot of automation and backward integration, which will give us superiority on product as well as the lowest cost and help us win in the market.

points.point: Asked by Vikash Jain (CLSA) whether the demerger was complete, Dinesh Taluja said it was still pending regulatory approvals — the only gating factor cited.
points.quote: Not yet, it is under regulatory approvals.

points.point: Anshuman Thakur gave the mechanics: it was a 100% subsidiary of RRVL that simply moves out, with shareholding mirrored so Reliance Retail shareholders hold the same stake.
points.quote: Today it is 100% sub of RRVL, it will just move out and shareholding will get replicated.

points.point: Demerger confirmed effective 1 December 2025, with RCPL's scale disclosed at over Rs 5,000 crore turnover, up 60% year on year, aided by brand acquisitions.
points.quote: On the FMCG side, the demerger happened on 1st December. And we are at more than 5,000 Crores of turnover, and this is 60% up on a year-on-year basis.

points.point: RCPL's exit was named as one of three factors in retail's 8.1% reported revenue growth: its full revenue sat in Q2 and has now left the retail P&L.
points.quote: And then the third part is the RCPL demerger, which was effective during the quarter. So RCPL's entire revenue was included in Q2. Now that revenue has gone out of retail business.

points.point: Harit Kapoor (Investec) pushed for the like-to-like growth and margin impact once the demerger hits a full quarter, estimating roughly a 1% revenue drag — analysts, not lenders or partners, drove the questioning.
points.quote: This is the first quarter where there is an RCPL demerger and from the next quarter it will be entirely there, so if you could just give us a sense of ex the merger what the like-to-like growth would be for the retail business and a little bit of back of the envelope suggests that it would be like a 1% impact

points.point: Management grouped the demerger with GST rationalization and the Q2/Q3 festive shift as short-term distortions to retail growth optics, not a change in the business's capability.
points.quote: it is a combination of things unique you do not have this Q2 and Q3 and some RCPL demerger and something to do with GST coming at the same time and accelerating from an EBITDA standpoint, accelerating on quick commerce, lots of things, so you have to see all that in context.

points.point: Retail's Rs 98,000 crore quarter grew 11% reported but almost 14% adjusted for the RCPL exit; full-year 12% would be higher excluding the demerger.
points.quote: Now, if you recollect, RCPL business was demerged out in the last quarter adjusted for that, the growth is almost 14%, for the full year the growth is 12% and if you exclude RCPL demerger the growth would be even higher.

points.point: First fully clean comparison: reported retail growth 7.4% versus 11.6% underlying once the RCPL exit is adjusted, with EBITDA margin 7.9%, down 80 bps, attributed to digital commerce mix rather than the demerger.
points.quote: In terms of topline growth, as you would recollect, RCPL business was demerged out on 1st of December. So Q1 had the full revenue. Adjusted for that, the underlying revenue growth is 11.6%. On a reported basis, the growth is 7.4%.

points.point: The filing text supplied as 'scheme rationale' contains no rationale for the RCPL/FMCG demerger at all — it is three unrelated Regulation 30 disclosures (the SevenHills Healthcare resolution plan, the STPL-into-JioStar merger effective 30 November 2025, and the Radisys Cayman merger). No rationale clauses can be cited from it.
points.quote: Jiostar has, on November 30, 2025 at 6:09 p.m. (IST), informed the Company that the said scheme has become effective from November 30, 2025 and STPL stands merged with Jiostar.

rationale.what_management_expects: RCPL/FMCG becomes a completely independent business under RIL, no longer inside retail, with its own distribution, world-class automated, backward-integrated manufacturing and R&D for product superiority and lowest cost, double-digit share in key markets and 60% growth; RRVL shareholding is replicated; retail's reported growth falls ~1%, with cleaner like-for-like growth of 11.6-14%.
rationale.gaps: No stated scheme rationale, tax/debt or asset allocation, valuation or listing plan, why RIL rather than retail holds it, lender or partner input, or RCPL profitability and capital needs.

segments.segment_name: RCPL (Reliance Consumer Products Limited) — the FMCG business, demerged from Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd. and a direct subsidiary of RIL from Dec 01, 2025
segments.measure_notes: No profit line is disclosed for RCPL anywhere in the tagged pages. RCPL/FMCG is not a reportable segment under Ind AS 108 — the four reported segments are O2C, Oil and Gas, Retail and Digital Services, and FMCG sits inside 'Others' (Presentation Apr 2026 p.8, p.11; Presentation Jan 2026 p.9), so no segment result/EBIT/EBITDA/PBT/PAT can be isolated. Revenue figures given are 'gross revenue' as labelled in the quarterly presentations (i.e. before netting of GST, and FY26 gross revenue 'includes RCPL sales before de-merger from RRVL'); they are not segment revenue reconciled to the financial statements.
